bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第060卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 60.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 60.

sentences.zh: 【漢紀五十二】起重光協洽，盡昭陽作噩，凡三年。

translations.literal: 【Han Records 52】 Beginning from Chongguang Xieqia through Zhaoyang Zuo'e—in all, three years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 52】 From the year Chongguang Xieqia through Zhaoyang Zuo'e—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinchou, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on xinchou day, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 關東諸將議：以朝廷幼沖，逼於董卓，遠隔關塞，不知存否，幽州牧劉虞，宗室賢俊，欲共立為主。

translations.literal: The generals east of the passes deliberated: because the court was young and tender, pressed by Dong Zhuo, and separated from them by the passes with no knowledge whether it still existed, Liu Yu, governor of You Province—a worthy man of the imperial clan—they wished jointly to establish as sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: The coalition commanders east of the passes debated installing Liu Yu, governor of You Province and a respected kinsman of the house, as emperor. The court was ruled by a child emperor hemmed in by Dong Zhuo, and cut off beyond the passes they could not even tell whether the sovereign still lived.

sentences.zh: 曹操曰：「吾等所以舉兵而遠近莫不響應者，以義故也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao said: "The reason we raised troops and none near or far failed to respond was righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "We took up arms and men rallied from every quarter because our cause was just.

sentences.zh: 今幼主微弱，制於奸臣，非有昌邑亡國之釁，而一旦改易，天下其孰安之！

translations.literal: Now the young ruler is feeble and controlled by treacherous ministers; there is not the portent of a kingdom's ruin as with Changyi, yet to change rulers at once—who under Heaven could be at ease!
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor is weak and in the grip of wicked ministers, but there is nothing like the Changyi affair that doomed a state. To replace him overnight—who in the realm would accept that?

sentences.zh: 諸君北面，我自西向。

translations.literal: You gentlemen may face north; I shall face west myself.
translations.idiomatic: You may bow to another lord—I will face west and remain loyal to Han.

sentences.zh: 」韓馥、袁紹以書與袁術曰：「帝非孝靈子，欲依絳、灌誅廢少主、迎立代王故事，奉大司馬虞為帝。

translations.literal: " Han Fu and Yuan Shao sent a letter to Yuan Shu saying: "The emperor is not a son of Emperor Xiaoling; wishing to follow the precedent of the Marquises of Jiang and Guan in deposing the young ruler and welcoming the King of Dai, they wish to enthrone Grand Marshal Yu as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu and Yuan Shao wrote Yuan Shu: "The present emperor is no son of Lingdi. Following the example of Jiang and Guan, who deposed a young ruler and installed the King of Dai, we propose to enthrone Liu Yu as Grand Marshal and emperor.

sentences.zh: 」術陰有不臣之心，不利國家有長君，乃外托公義以拒之。

translations.literal: " Yuan Shu secretly harbored disloyal intentions and did not wish the state to have a mature ruler; he therefore outwardly invoked public righteousness to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu secretly coveted the throne himself and disliked a strong sovereign for the realm, so he refused on the pretext of loyalty to Han.

sentences.zh: 紹復與術書曰：「今西名有幼君，無血脈之屬，公卿以下皆媚事卓，安可覆信！

translations.literal: Shao again wrote to Shu: "Now in the west there is nominally a young ruler with no blood tie; from the ministers down all fawn on Zhuo—how can faith be placed in them!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao wrote again: "Out west there is only a child on the throne who is no true heir. Every official grovels before Zhuo. Why trust them?

sentences.zh: 但當使兵往屯關要，皆自蹙死。

translations.literal: One need only send troops to hold the strategic passes—they will all perish by their own strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Send troops to block the passes and they will squeeze themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 東立聖君，太平可冀，如何有疑？

translations.literal: Establish a sage ruler in the east, and peace may be hoped for—why any doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Install a true sovereign in the east and order can be restored—what is there to hesitate over?

sentences.zh: 又室家見戮，不念子胥可復北面乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, your household was slaughtered—do you not recall how Wu Zixu could never again face north?
translations.idiomatic: Your own kin were butchered. Have you forgotten Zixu, who could never again bow north to his enemy?

sentences.zh: 」術答曰：「聖主聰睿，有周成之質。

translations.literal: " Shu replied: "The sage ruler is wise and perceptive, possessing the qualities of King Cheng of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu replied, "Our sovereign is intelligent and wise, with the makings of King Cheng of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 賊卓因危亂之際，威服百寮，此乃漢家小厄之會，乃雲今上『無血脈之屬』，豈不誣乎！

translations.literal: The rebel Zhuo exploited a time of crisis to awe the hundred officials into submission—this is but a minor trial of the Han house; to say the present sovereign has 'no blood tie'—is that not slander!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo exploited chaos to cow the court—that is Han's misfortune, not grounds to call our emperor illegitimate. To claim he has 'no royal blood' is a lie!

sentences.zh: 又曰『室家見戮，可復北面』，此卓所為，豈國家哉！

translations.literal: Again you say 'your household was slaughtered—can you face north again'—that was Zhuo's doing; is that the state's affair!
translations.idiomatic: As for my family's slaughter—that was Zhuo's crime, not the state's. How dare you use it against loyalty to the throne!

sentences.zh: 慺慺赤心，志在滅卓，不識其他！

translations.literal: Earnestly and sincerely my red heart is set on destroying Zhuo; I know nothing else!
translations.idiomatic: My sole aim is to destroy Zhuo. I will hear nothing else!

sentences.zh: 」馥、紹竟遣故樂浪太守張岐等繼議上虞尊號。

translations.literal: " Fu and Shao still sent the former governor of Lelang Zhang Qi and others to continue pressing Liu Yu to accept the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless Han Fu and Yuan Shao sent the former governor of Lelang Zhang Qi and others to press Liu Yu to accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 虞見岐等，厲色叱之曰：「今天下崩亂，主上蒙塵，吾被重恩，未能清雪國恥。

translations.literal: Yu saw Qi and the others and sharply rebuked them: "Now the realm is collapsing in disorder; the sovereign suffers in the dust; I have received great favor yet have been unable to wipe away the nation's shame.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu met Zhang Qi and his party, he sternly reproached them: "The empire is in chaos and the emperor in distress. I owe the throne deep gratitude yet have not avenged our disgrace.

sentences.zh: 諸君各據州郡，宜共戮力盡心王室，而反造逆謀以相垢污邪！

translations.literal: You gentlemen each hold commanderies and prefectures—you ought to join your strength in loyalty to the royal house, yet instead you hatch treasonous schemes to besmirch me!
translations.idiomatic: You hold provinces and commanderies—you should unite to serve the Han. Why scheme treason and slander me?

sentences.zh: 」固拒之。

translations.literal: " He firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 馥等又請虞領尚書事，承製封拜，復不聽，欲奔匈奴以自絕，紹等乃止。

translations.literal: Fu and the others also asked Yu to head the Masters of Writing affairs and issue edicts for enfeoffment and appointment; again he would not listen and wished to flee to the Xiongnu to cut himself off—only then did Shao and the rest stop.
translations.idiomatic: They asked him to preside over the Secretariat and issue imperial appointments; again he refused. He threatened to flee to the Xiongnu rather than comply, and at last Yuan Shao and the others desisted.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁丑，以董卓為太師，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day dingchou, Dong Zhuo was made Grand Preceptor, his rank placed above all feudal kings.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingchou day, Dong Zhuo was appointed Grand Preceptor with rank above all princes.

sentences.zh: 孫堅移屯梁東，為卓將徐榮所敗，復收散卒進屯陽人。

translations.literal: Sun Jian moved his camp to Liangdong and was defeated by Zhuo's general Xu Rong; he gathered his scattered troops again and advanced to camp at Yangren.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian shifted his camp to Liangdong, was beaten by Dong Zhuo's general Xu Rong, regrouped his scattered forces, and encamped at Yangren.

sentences.zh: 卓遣東郡太守胡軫督步騎五千擊之，以呂布為騎督。

translations.literal: Zhuo sent the governor of Dong commandery Hu Zhen to direct five thousand foot and horse to attack him, with Lü Bu as cavalry commander.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sent the governor of Dong commandery Hu Zhen with five thousand infantry and cavalry against him, with Lü Bu commanding the horse.

sentences.zh: 軫與布不相得，堅出擊，大破之，梟其都督華雄。

translations.literal: Zhen and Bu did not get along; Jian sallied forth and routed them heavily, beheading their commander Hua Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhen and Lü Bu quarreled. Sun Jian attacked, won a great victory, and beheaded the enemy commander Hua Xiong.

sentences.zh: 或謂袁術曰：「堅若得雒，不可複製，此為除狼而得虎也。

translations.literal: Someone told Yuan Shu: "If Jian takes Luoyang, he cannot be controlled again—this is driving out wolves and getting tigers."
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Yuan Shu: "If Sun Jian seizes Luoyang you will never control him again—you would trade wolves for a tiger."

sentences.zh: 」術疑之，不運軍糧。

translations.literal: " Shu grew suspicious and stopped forwarding army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu grew suspicious and cut off his supplies.

sentences.zh: 堅夜馳見術，畫地計校曰：「所以出身不顧者，上為國家討賊，下慰將軍家門之私讎。

translations.literal: Jian galloped by night to see Shu, traced diagrams on the ground and reckoned: "The reason I risk my life is above to punish rebels for the state, below to console your family's private vendetta.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian rode to Yuan Shu by night, sketched plans on the ground, and said, "I risk everything first to serve the state against rebels, and second to avenge your family's private wrongs.

sentences.zh: 堅與卓非有骨肉之怨也，而將軍受浸潤之言，還相嫌疑，何也？

translations.literal: Jian and Zhuo have no kin hatred, yet the general listens to insinuations and turns to mutual suspicion—why?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo and I have no feud of blood—why let slander make us doubt each other?

sentences.zh: 」術踧踖，即調發軍糧。

translations.literal: " Shu was abashed and immediately ordered army grain dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu was ashamed and immediately sent provisions.

sentences.zh: 堅還屯，卓遣將軍李傕說堅，欲與和親，令堅疏子弟任刺史、郡守者，許表用之。

translations.literal: Jian returned to camp; Zhuo sent the general Li Jue to persuade Jian, wishing alliance by marriage, and directed Jian to list relatives and sons serving as regional inspectors and commandery governors—promising to recommend them for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian returned to camp. Dong Zhuo sent Li Jue to offer alliance and marriage, promising to appoint Sun Jian's relatives who held provincial and commandery posts.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「卓逆天無道，今不夷汝三族，縣示四海，則吾死不瞑目，豈將與乃和親邪！

translations.literal: Jian said: "Zhuo defies Heaven and is without the Way; if I do not exterminate your three clans and display them to the four seas, I shall not close my eyes in death—how would I make alliance with you!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian replied: "Zhuo defies Heaven and violates all law. Unless I wipe out your whole clan and display it to the empire I cannot die in peace. Why would I ally with you?

sentences.zh: 」復進軍大谷，距雒九十里。

translations.literal: " He advanced again to Dagu, ninety li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on to Dagu, ninety li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 卓自出，與堅戰於諸陵間。

translations.literal: Zhuo came out in person and fought Jian among the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo came out in person and fought Sun Jian among the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 卓敗走，卻屯澠池，聚兵於陝。

translations.literal: Zhuo was defeated and fled, withdrawing to camp at Mianchi and gathering troops at Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo was routed, withdrew to Mianchi, and concentrated forces at Shaan.

sentences.zh: 堅進至雒陽，擊呂布，復破走。

translations.literal: Jian advanced to Luoyang, struck Lü Bu, and routed him again.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian pressed into Luoyang, attacked Lü Bu, and drove him off again.

sentences.zh: 堅乃掃除宗廟，祠以太牢，得傳國璽於城南甄宮井中；

translations.literal: Jian then swept and cleaned the ancestral temples, sacrificed with the grand victim, and obtained the imperial heirloom seal from the well of Zhen Palace south of the city;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian restored the ancestral temples, offered the grand sacrifice, and recovered the imperial jade seal from the well of Zhen Palace south of the city;

sentences.zh: 分兵出新安、澠池間以邀卓。

translations.literal: he divided troops to emerge between Xin'an and Mianchi to intercept Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: then sent detachments through Xin'an and Mianchi to ambush Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓謂長史劉艾曰：「關東軍敗數矣，皆畏孤，無能為也。

translations.literal: Zhuo said to his chief clerk Liu Ai: "The armies east of the passes have been defeated several times; all fear me and can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo told his chief clerk Liu Ai: "The eastern coalition has lost battle after battle. They all fear me and are harmless.

sentences.zh: 惟孫堅小戇，頗能用人，當語諸將，使知忌之。

translations.literal: Only Sun Jian is somewhat rash yet fairly good at using men—you should tell the generals to know fear of him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sun Jian is rash but knows how to use men. Tell the generals to beware of him.

sentences.zh: 孤昔與周慎西征邊、韓於金城，孤語張溫，求引所將兵為慎作後駐，溫不聽。

translations.literal: Long ago I campaigned west with Zhou Shen against Bian Zhang and Han Sui at Jincheng; I told Zhang Wen, asking to lead my troops as Shen's rear guard—Wen would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Once on campaign with Zhou Shen against Bian Zhang and Han Sui at Jincheng, I asked Zhang Wen to let me hold the rear with my troops. Wen refused.

sentences.zh: 溫又使孤討先零叛羌，孤知其不克而不得止，遂行，留別部司馬劉靖將步騎四千屯安定以為聲勢。

translations.literal: Wen also sent me to subdue the traitorous Qiang of Xianling; I knew it would not succeed yet could not stop, and so went, leaving the detached division marshal Liu Jing with four thousand foot and horse at Anding as a show of force.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then ordered me against the rebellious Xianling Qiang. I knew we would fail but had to go, leaving Liu Jing with four thousand men at Anding as a deterrent.

sentences.zh: 叛羌欲截歸道，孤小擊輒開，畏安定有兵故也。

translations.literal: The rebel Qiang wished to cut my return route; a small strike from me and they opened the way—the reason was their fear of troops at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels meant to cut my retreat, but a small blow from me opened the road—they feared the force at Anding.

sentences.zh: 虜謂安定當數萬人，不知但靖也。

translations.literal: The barbarians thought Anding had tens of thousands of men, not knowing it was only Jing.
translations.idiomatic: They thought tens of thousands held Anding, not knowing it was only Liu Jing.

sentences.zh: 而孫堅隨周慎行，謂慎求先將萬兵造金城，使慎以二萬作後駐。

translations.literal: Sun Jian marched with Zhou Shen and told Shen to ask to lead ten thousand men first to Jincheng, letting Shen hold twenty thousand as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian campaigned with Zhou Shen and urged him to send ten thousand men ahead to Jincheng while Shen held twenty thousand in reserve.

sentences.zh: 邊、韓畏慎大兵，不敢輕與堅戰，而堅兵足以斷其運道。

translations.literal: Bian and Han feared Shen's great army and dared not lightly fight Jian, while Jian's troops sufficed to cut their supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and Han would have feared Shen's main force and avoided Sun Jian, while Sun Jian could have severed their supply lines.

sentences.zh: 兒曹用其言，涼州或能定也。

translations.literal: Had those boys used his counsel, Liang province might have been settled.
translations.idiomatic: Had they listened, Liang province might have been pacified.

sentences.zh: 溫既不能用孤，慎又不能用堅，卒用敗走。

translations.literal: Wen would not use me, Shen would not use Jian—in the end they were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wen ignored me, Shen ignored Sun Jian, and in the end they were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 堅以佐軍司馬，所見略與人同，固自為可；

translations.literal: Jian as assistant army marshal—his views are roughly the same as others', and he certainly thinks himself capable;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian was only an assistant army marshal, yet his judgment matched any man's—he thinks himself quite able—

sentences.zh: 但無故從諸袁兒，終亦死耳！

translations.literal: but for no reason he follows the Yuan boys—in the end he too will die!
translations.idiomatic: yet he follows the Yuan clan for no good reason. In the end he will die like the rest!

sentences.zh: 」乃使東中郎將董越屯澠池，中郎將段煨屯華陰，中郎將牛輔屯安邑，其餘諸將布在諸縣，以御山東。

translations.literal: " He then posted the eastern gentlemen-of-the-household-general Dong Yue at Mianchi, the gentleman-of-the-household-general Duan Wei at Huayin, the gentleman-of-the-household-general Niu Fu at Anyi, and the rest of the generals spread through the commanderies to guard against the east.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed Dong Yue at Mianchi, Duan Wei at Huayin, Niu Fu at Anyi, and dispersed other officers through the counties to block the east.

sentences.zh: 輔，卓之婿也。

translations.literal: Fu was Zhuo's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Fu was Dong Zhuo's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 卓引還長安。

translations.literal: Zhuo withdrew to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo withdrew to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 孫堅修塞諸陵，引軍還魯陽。

translations.literal: Sun Jian repaired the imperial tombs and led his army back to Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian restored the tombs and marched back to Luyang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，董卓至長安，公卿皆迎拜車下。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Dong Zhuo reached Chang'an; the ministers and nobles all welcomed and bowed beneath his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Dong Zhuo arrived at Chang'an. Every minister bowed beneath his carriage.

sentences.zh: 卓抵手謂御史中丞皇甫嵩曰：「義真，怖未乎？

translations.literal: Zhuo clapped his hands and said to the imperial attendant grandee Huangfu Song: "Yizhen, are you frightened yet?
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo clapped Huangfu Song on the shoulder and asked, "Yizhen, are you afraid yet?

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「明公以德輔朝廷，大慶方至，何怖之有！

translations.literal: " Song said: "Your Excellency assists the court with virtue; great rejoicing is at hand—what is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Song replied, "Your Excellency supports the court with virtue. Good fortune is coming—why should I fear?

sentences.zh: 若淫刑以逞，將天下皆懼，豈獨嵩乎！

translations.literal: If cruel punishments are indulged to the full, then all under Heaven will fear—how would it be only Song!
translations.idiomatic: But if you indulge cruel punishments, the whole world will tremble—not I alone!

sentences.zh: 」卓黨欲尊卓比太公，稱尚父。

translations.literal: " Zhuo's faction wished to honor Zhuo like the Grand Duke, calling him Esteemed Father.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's followers wished to compare him to the Duke of Zhou and style him Esteemed Father.

sentences.zh: 卓以問蔡邕，邕曰：「明公威德，誠為巍巍，然比之太公，愚意以為未可。

translations.literal: Zhuo asked Cai Yong; Yong said: "Your Excellency's authority and virtue are truly lofty, yet to compare with the Grand Duke—in my humble opinion it cannot yet be done.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo consulted Cai Yong, who said, "Your authority is immense, but the comparison with the Duke of Zhou is premature.

sentences.zh: 宜須關東平定，車駕還反舊京，然後議之。

translations.literal: One ought to wait until east of the passes is settled and the imperial carriage returns to the old capital—then discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the east is pacified and the emperor returns to Luoyang—then consider it.

sentences.zh: 」卓乃止。

translations.literal: " Zhuo then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 卓使司隸校尉劉器籍吏民有為子不孝、為臣不忠、為吏不清、為弟不順者，皆身誅，財物沒官。

translations.literal: Zhuo had the colonel of the masters of writing Liu Qi register officials and commoners guilty of unfilial sons, disloyal ministers, corrupt clerks, or unfilial younger brothers—all were executed in person and property confiscated to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo had Liu Qi the metropolitan governor register citizens guilty of unfilial sons, disloyal subjects, corrupt officials, or unruly brothers. All were executed and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 於是更相誣引，冤死者以千數。

translations.literal: Thereupon mutual denunciation followed, and innocents wrongly killed numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Accusers denounced one another, and thousands died unjustly.

sentences.zh: 百姓囂囂，道路以目。

translations.literal: The common people were in uproar; they met eyes on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The people seethed in fear; no one dared speak on the road.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙戌，地震。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day bingxu, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingxu day, an earthquake struck.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，司空種拂免；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Zhong Fu was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Minister of Works Zhong Fu was removed;

sentences.zh: 以光祿大夫濟南淳於嘉為司空，太尉趙謙罷；

translations.literal: the grandee of bright rank Chunyu Jia of Jinan was made Minister of Works, and Grand Commandant Zhao Qian was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Jia of Jinan, grandee of bright rank, was appointed Minister of Works, and Grand Commandant Zhao Qian was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 以太常馬日磾為太尉。

translations.literal: the minister of imperial sacrifices Ma Midi was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Midi, minister of imperial sacrifices, became Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 初，何進遣雲中張楊還并州募兵，會進敗，楊留上黨，有眾數千人。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Jin had sent Zhang Yang of Yunzhong back to Bing province to raise troops; when Jin was defeated, Yang remained at Shangdang with several thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier He Jin had sent Zhang Yang of Yunzhong to Bing province to raise troops. When He Jin fell, Yang stayed at Shangdang with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 袁紹在河內，楊往歸之，與南單于於扶羅屯漳水。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao was at Henei; Yang went to join him, and with the southern Chanyu Yufuluo encamped on the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao was at Henei. Zhang Yang joined him and camped on the Zhang River with the southern Chanyu Yufuluo.

sentences.zh: 韓馥以豪傑多歸心袁紹，忌之；

translations.literal: Han Fu, because many heroes' hearts turned to Yuan Shao, was jealous of him;
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu saw that many leaders looked to Yuan Shao and grew jealous;

sentences.zh: 陰貶節其軍糧，欲使其眾離散。

translations.literal: he secretly reduced and curbed his army grain, wishing to make his troops scatter.
translations.idiomatic: he secretly cut Yuan Shao's rations, hoping to break up his army.

sentences.zh: 會馥將麴義叛，馥與戰而敗，紹因與義相結。

translations.literal: Just then Fu's general Qu Yi rebelled; Fu fought him and was defeated, and Shao thereupon allied with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu's general Qu Yi rebelled, Fu fought and lost. Yuan Shao then allied with Qu Yi.

sentences.zh: 紹客逢紀謂紹曰：「將軍舉大事而仰人資結，不據一州，無以自全。

translations.literal: Shao's retainer Pang Ji said to Shao: "The general raises a great enterprise yet depends on others for supplies—you must hold a province or you cannot preserve yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji told Yuan Shao: "You have undertaken a great cause yet depend on others for supplies. Unless you hold a province you cannot survive."

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「冀州兵強，吾士饑乏，設不能辦，無所容立。

translations.literal: " Shao said: "Ji Province's troops are strong, my men hungry and lacking—if we cannot manage it, there is nowhere to stand."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao replied: "Ji Province's armies are strong and my men are starving. If we fail, we have nowhere to go."

sentences.zh: 」紀曰：「韓馥庸才，可密要公孫瓚使取冀州，馥必駭懼，因遣辯士為陳禍福，馥迫於倉卒，必肯遜讓。

translations.literal: " Ji said: "Han Fu is a mediocrity—secretly invite Gongsun Zan to seize Ji Province; Fu will be terrified, and then send an eloquent man to lay out fortune and disaster; Fu, pressed in haste, is sure to yield."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji said: "Han Fu is a mediocrity. Secretly urge Gongsun Zan to attack Ji Province. Fu will panic, and when our envoys explain the alternatives he will yield in haste."

sentences.zh: 」紹然之，即以書與瓚。

translations.literal: " Shao approved and at once sent a letter to Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao agreed and wrote to Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 瓚遂引兵而至，外托討董卓而陰謀襲馥，馥與戰不利。

translations.literal: Zan thereupon led his troops thither, outwardly citing campaign against Dong Zhuo while secretly plotting to strike Fu; Fu fought him unsuccessfully.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan marched south, ostensibly against Dong Zhuo but secretly to seize Ji from Han Fu, who fought him and lost.

sentences.zh: 會董卓入關，紹還軍延津，使外甥陳留高幹及馥所親穎川辛評、荀諶、郭圖等說馥曰：「公孫瓚將燕、代之卒乘勝來南，而諸郡應之，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Just then Zhuo entered the passes; Shao returned his army to Yanjin and sent his nephew Chenliu Gao Gan and Fu's intimates Yingchuan Xin Ping, Xun Chen, Guo Tu and others to persuade Fu: "Gongsun Zan is leading Yan and Dai troops south on a winning march, and the commanderies are responding—his edge cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo entered the passes Yuan Shao withdrew to Yanjin and sent his nephew Gao Gan plus Han Fu's advisers Xin Ping, Xun Chen, and Guo Tu to warn him: "Gongsun Zan is driving his Yan and Dai veterans south in victory, and the commanderies are rallying to him. You cannot stop him.

sentences.zh: 袁車騎引軍東向，其意未可量也。

translations.literal: Yuan the chariot-and-horse general leads his army eastward—his intentions cannot be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is marching east as well. His intentions are unknown."

sentences.zh: 竊為將軍危之！

translations.literal: I privately fear for the general's peril!
translations.idiomatic: I fear for your safety, General!

sentences.zh: 」馥懼，曰：「然則為之奈何？

translations.literal: " Fu was afraid and said: "Then what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu asked, "What then should I do?

sentences.zh: 」諶曰：「君自料寬仁容眾為天下所附，孰與袁氏？

translations.literal: " Chen said: "Does the lord reckon himself superior to the Yuan clan in breadth and kindness that win all hearts?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chen asked, "Do you consider yourself more beloved for your generosity than the Yuan clan?"

sentences.zh: 」馥曰：「不如也。

translations.literal: " Fu said: "I am not their equal."
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu said, "No."

sentences.zh: 」「監危吐決，智勇過人，又孰與袁氏？

translations.literal: "In reading danger and deciding crises, in wisdom and courage surpassing others—again, who compares with the Yuan?"
translations.idiomatic: In reading danger and acting decisively—in wisdom and courage—who compares with the Yuan?

sentences.zh: 」馥曰：「不如也。

translations.literal: " Fu said: "I am not their equal."
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu said, "Not I."

sentences.zh: 」諶曰：「袁氏一時之傑，將軍資三不如之勢，久處其上，彼必不為將軍下也。

translations.literal: " Chen said: "The Yuan are heroes of the age; the general, with three disadvantages, has long sat above them—they surely will not remain below the general."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chen said, "The Yuan are the leading men of the day. You have admitted three inferiorities yet have long ranked above them. They will not serve under you forever."

sentences.zh: 夫冀州，天下之重資也，彼若與公孫瓚並力取之，危亡可立而待也。

translations.literal: Ji Province is the realm's heavy resource; if they join Gongsun Zan in strength to take it, peril and destruction can await at once."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province is the empire's treasure house. If they join Gongsun Zan against you, your fall will be swift."

sentences.zh: 夫袁氏，將軍之舊，且為同盟，當今之計，若舉冀州以讓袁氏，彼必厚德將軍，瓚亦不能與之爭矣。

translations.literal: The Yuan are the general's old acquaintance and allies besides; the present plan—if you raise Ji Province to yield to the Yuan, they will surely treat the general generously, and Zan cannot contend with them."
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan are your old allies. Yield Ji Province to Yuan Shao. He will reward you generously and Gongsun Zan cannot challenge him."

sentences.zh: 是將軍有讓賢之名，而身安於泰山也。

translations.literal: Thus the general gains the fame of yielding to the worthy, and your person rests secure as Mount Tai."
translations.idiomatic: You gain fame for gracious humility and stand secure as Mount Tai."

sentences.zh: 」馥性恇怯，因然其計。

translations.literal: " Fu was timid by nature and therefore approved this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu was timid by nature and accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 馥長史耿武、別駕閔純、治中李歷聞而諫曰：「冀州帶甲百萬，谷支十年。

translations.literal: Fu's chief clerk Geng Wu, separate carriage attendant Min Chun, and administration officer Li Li heard and remonstrated: "Ji Province has a million armored men and grain for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Geng Wu, attendant Min Chun, and administration officer Li Li protested: "Ji Province has a million armed men and ten years of grain.

sentences.zh: 袁紹孤客窮軍，仰我鼻息，譬如嬰兒在股掌之上，絕其哺乳，立可餓殺，奈何欲以州與之！

translations.literal: Yuan Shao is a lone guest with a destitute army, breathing through our nostrils—like an infant on the palm; stop its nursing and it can be starved to death at once—why give the province to him!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is a homeless guest with a broken army living on our breath—like an infant in our palm. Cut off his supplies and he starves at once. Why surrender the province to him?

sentences.zh: 」馥曰：「吾袁氏故吏，且才不如本初，度德而讓，古人所貴，諸君獨何病焉！

translations.literal: " Fu said: "I am an old subordinate of the Yuan clan, and my talent is not equal to Benchu's—measuring virtue and yielding is prized by the ancients; why do you gentlemen alone find fault!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu said, "I am an old servant of the Yuan. My talent falls short of Benchu's. To yield by measure of virtue is what antiquity honors—why do you object?"

sentences.zh: 」先是，馥從事趙浮、程渙將強弩萬張屯孟津，聞之，率兵馳還。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Fu's attendant Zhao Fu and Cheng Huan had led ten thousand strong crossbows stationed at Mengjin; on hearing this, they led troops galloping back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his attendants Zhao Fu and Cheng Huan had ten thousand crossbowmen at Mengjin; hearing the plan, they hurried back.

sentences.zh: 時紹在朝歌清水，浮等從後來，船數百艘，眾萬餘人，整兵鼓，夜過紹營，紹甚惡之。

translations.literal: At the time Shao was at Chaoge on the Qing River; Fu and the others came from behind—hundreds of boats, more than ten thousand men, drilling troops and beating drums, passing Shao's camp by night; Shao greatly detested it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao was at Chaoge on the Qing River when Zhao Fu and Cheng Huan came up behind with hundreds of boats, more than ten thousand men, drums beating, marching past Yuan Shao's camp by night. He was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 浮等到，謂馥曰：「袁本初軍無頭糧，各已離散，雖有張楊、於扶羅新附，未肯為用，不足敵也。

translations.literal: When Fu and the others arrived they told Fu: "Yuan Benchu's army lacks grain at the head, each has scattered; though Zhang Yang and Yufuluo have newly attached, they are unwilling to be used—not enough to oppose us."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fu and Cheng Huan told Han Fu: "Yuan Shao's army has no grain. His followers are scattering. Zhang Yang and Yufuluo have just joined him but will not fight for him. He is no match for us."

sentences.zh: 小從事等請以見兵拒之，旬日之間，必土崩瓦解。

translations.literal: We junior attendants ask to resist him with the troops at hand—in ten days or so he will surely crumble and disperse."
translations.idiomatic: Let us oppose him with the forces at hand. Within ten days he will collapse."

sentences.zh: 明將軍但當開閣高枕，何憂何懼！

translations.literal: Illustrious general, you need only open your doors and sleep on high pillows—what worry, what fear!
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious General, you need only reopen your doors and rest easy—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 」馥又不聽，乃避位，出居中常侍趙忠故捨，遣子送印綬以讓紹。

translations.literal: " Fu again would not listen; he then vacated his post, moved out to the former residence of the regular palace attendant Zhao Zhong, and sent his son with the seal and cord to yield to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu refused again. He vacated his office, moved into the former house of Zhao Zhong, and sent his son with the provincial seal to surrender to Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹將至，從事十人爭棄馥去，獨耿武、閔純杖刀拒之，不能禁，乃止；

translations.literal: When Shao was about to arrive, ten attendants vied to abandon Fu and leave; only Geng Wu and Min Chun brandished blades to resist and could not stop them, and so ceased;
translations.idiomatic: As Yuan Shao approached, ten of Fu's staff fled. Only Geng Wu and Min Chun drew blades to block them but could not, and gave up;

sentences.zh: 紹皆殺之。

translations.literal: Shao had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 紹遂領冀州牧，承製以馥為奮威將軍，而無所將御，亦無官屬。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon took office as governor of Ji Province; by imperial rescript he made Fu General Who Displays Might, but Fu had no troops to command and no staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao took office as governor of Ji Province and appointed Han Fu General Who Displays Might, but Fu commanded no troops and had no staff.

sentences.zh: 紹以廣平沮授為奮武將軍，使監護諸將，寵遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Shao appointed Ju Shou of Guangping as General Who Displays Martial Power, to oversee and protect the generals, treating him with very great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao made Ju Shou of Guangping General Who Displays Martial Power to oversee his commanders and favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 魏郡審配、巨鹿田豐並以正直不得志於韓馥，紹以豐為別駕，配為治中，及南陽許攸、逢紀、穎川荀諶皆為謀主。

translations.literal: Shen Pei of Wei commandery and Tian Feng of Julu, both upright men who had not prospered under Han Fu—Shao made Feng separate carriage attendant and Pei administration officer; and Xu You of Nanyang, Pang Ji, and Xun Chen of Yingchuan all became chief strategists.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei of Wei and Tian Feng of Julu, upright men who had failed under Han Fu, became Yuan Shao's chief advisers, along with Xu You, Pang Ji, and Xun Chen.

sentences.zh: 紹以河內朱漢為都官從事。

translations.literal: Shao appointed Zhu Han of Henei as director of the masters of writing for legal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao appointed Zhu Han of Henei director of legal affairs.

sentences.zh: 漢先為韓馥所不禮，且欲徼迎紹意，擅發兵圍守馥第，拔刃登屋，馥走上樓，收得馥大兒，槌折兩腳。

translations.literal: Han had earlier been treated discourteously by Han Fu and wished to curry Shao's favor; he sent troops on his own authority to surround Fu's residence, drew blades and climbed the roof; Fu fled upstairs; Han seized Fu's eldest son and beat both his legs broken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Han had been slighted by Han Fu and sought Yuan Shao's favor. He surrounded Fu's house without orders, climbed the roof with drawn blades, and when Fu fled upstairs seized his eldest son and broke both his legs.

sentences.zh: 紹立收漢，殺之。

translations.literal: Shao at once arrested Han and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao immediately arrested Zhu Han and executed him.

sentences.zh: 馥猶憂怖，從紹索去，往依張邈。

translations.literal: Fu was still fearful; he begged Shao to let him leave and went to rely on Zhang Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu remained terrified. He asked Yuan Shao for permission to leave and went to join Zhang Miao.

sentences.zh: 後紹遣使詣邈，有所計議，與邈耳語；

translations.literal: Later Shao sent an envoy to Miao to discuss plans; he whispered in Miao's ear;
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Shao sent an envoy to Zhang Miao for counsel and spoke with him in a whisper;

sentences.zh: 馥在坐上，謂為見圖，無何，起至溷，以書刀自殺。

translations.literal: Fu was present at the gathering; thinking he was plotted against, before long he rose, went to the privy, and killed himself with a writing knife.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu was in attendance and thought they were plotting against him. Soon he rose, went to the latrine, and killed himself with a letter opener.

sentences.zh: 鮑信謂曹操曰：「袁紹為盟主，因權奪利，將自生亂，是復有一卓也。

translations.literal: Bao Xin said to Cao Cao: "Yuan Shao as alliance chief abuses power to seize profit; he will bring turmoil on himself—there is another Dong Zhuo."
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xin told Cao Cao, "Yuan Shao leads the coalition but exploits his rank for gain. He will breed chaos in his own camp—we would simply have another Dong Zhuo."

sentences.zh: 若抑之，則力不能制，只以遘難。

translations.literal: If we restrain him, our strength cannot control him—we would only meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: If you try to check him now, we lack the strength to control him and would only invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 且可規大河之南以待其變。

translations.literal: Moreover we may scheme for the land south of the great river and await his changes.
translations.idiomatic: Better to secure territory south of the Yellow River and wait for events to turn.

sentences.zh: 」操善之。

translations.literal: " Cao approved.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 會黑山、於毒、白繞、眭固等十餘萬眾人略東郡，王肱不能御。

translations.literal: It happened that the Black Mountain band, Yu Du, Bai Rao, Sui Gu, and more than a hundred thousand men raided Dong commandery; Wang Gong could not repel them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Black Mountain rebels under Yu Du, Bai Rao, Sui Gu, and others—more than a hundred thousand strong—ravaged Dong commandery, and the governor Wang Gong could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 曹操引兵入東郡，擊白繞於濮陽，破之。

translations.literal: Cao Cao led troops into Dong commandery, struck Bai Rao at Puyang, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched into Dong commandery, attacked Bai Rao at Puyang, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 袁紹因表操為東郡太守，治東武陽。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao thereupon memorialized that Cao be made grand administrator of Dong commandery, with his seat at Dong Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao recommended Cao Cao as grand administrator of Dong commandery, with his headquarters at Dong Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 南單于劫張楊以叛袁紹，屯於黎陽。

translations.literal: The Southern Xiongnu chanyu seized Zhang Yang to rebel against Yuan Shao and encamped at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu abducted Zhang Yang and rebelled against Yuan Shao, camping at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 董卓以楊為建義將軍、河內太守。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo made Yang General Who Establishes Righteousness and grand administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo appointed Zhang Yang General Who Establishes Righteousness and governor of Henei.

sentences.zh: 太史望氣，言當有大臣戮死者。

translations.literal: The astrologer observing qi said a great minister would die by execution.
translations.idiomatic: Court astrologers reading the heavens predicted that a great minister would be put to death.

sentences.zh: 董卓使人誣衛尉張溫與袁術交通，冬，十月，壬戌，笞殺溫於市以應之。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo sent men to accuse Commandant of Guards Zhang Wen of communicating with Yuan Shu; in winter, the tenth month, on the day renxu, Wen was flogged to death in the market to fulfill the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo fabricated charges that Commandant of Guards Zhang Wen was conspiring with Yuan Shu. On the renxu day of the tenth winter month, he had Wen flogged to death in the marketplace to fulfill the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 青州黃巾寇勃海，眾三十萬，欲與黑山合。

translations.literal: Qing province Yellow Turbans raided Bohai; their host was three hundred thousand; they wished to join the Black Mountain band.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Turban rebels from Qing province invaded Bohai with three hundred thousand men, intending to link up with the Black Mountain forces.

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚率步騎二萬人逆擊於東光南，大破之，斬首三萬餘級。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan led twenty thousand foot and horse to meet the attack south of Dongguang, crushing them and taking more than thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to intercept them south of Dongguang, winning a great victory and claiming more than thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 賊棄其輜重，奔走渡河。

translations.literal: The bandits abandoned their baggage trains and fled in haste across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels abandoned their wagons and fled across the river.

sentences.zh: 瓚因其半濟薄之，賊復大破，死者數萬，流血丹水，收得生口七萬餘人，車甲財物不可勝算，威名大震。

translations.literal: Zan took advantage of their half-crossing to press them; the bandits were again crushed; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands; blood reddened the waters; captives taken exceeded seventy thousand; chariots, armor, and goods beyond counting—his renown shook all.
translations.idiomatic: Zan struck while they were half across the river and shattered them again. Tens of thousands died, the water ran red, and he took more than seventy thousand captives along with countless chariots, armor, and loot. His fame soared.

sentences.zh: 劉虞子和為侍中，帝思東歸，使和偽逃董卓，潛出武關詣虞，令將兵來迎。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's son He was a palace attendant; the emperor thought of returning east; he had He feign flight from Dong Zhuo, slip out through Wu Pass to Yu, and order him to bring troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He, son of Liu Yu, served as palace attendant. The emperor hoped to return east and sent He to feign escape from Dong Zhuo, slip out through Wu Pass to his father, and summon troops to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 和至南陽，袁術利虞為援，留和不遣，許兵至俱西，令和為書與虞。

translations.literal: When He reached Nanyang, Yuan Shu, coveting Yu as ally, detained He; he promised that when troops arrived they would go west together, and had He write to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu He reached Nanyang, Yuan Shu, wanting Liu Yu's support, detained him, promising to march west together once troops arrived, and had He write to his father.

sentences.zh: 虞得書，遣數千騎詣和。

translations.literal: Yu received the letter and sent several thousand horsemen to He.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu received the letter and dispatched several thousand cavalry to meet his son.

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚知術有異志，止之，虞不聽。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan knew Shu had irregular ambitions and stopped him; Yu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan, knowing Yuan Shu's designs, urged Liu Yu to stop, but Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 瓚恐術聞而怨之，亦遣其從弟越將千騎詣術。

translations.literal: Zan feared that if Shu heard of this he would resent him; he also sent his cousin Yue leading a thousand horse to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid Yuan Shu would resent him, Gongsun Zan also sent his cousin Gongsun Yue with a thousand cavalry to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 而陰教術執和，奪其兵，由是虞、瓚有隙。

translations.literal: Yet in secret he instructed Shu to seize He and take his troops; from this Yu and Zan had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he urged Yuan Shu to seize Liu He and take his troops. From this Liu Yu and Gongsun Zan fell out.

sentences.zh: 和逃術來北，復為袁紹所留。

translations.literal: He fled Shu and came north, but was again detained by Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He escaped Yuan Shu and headed north, only to be detained again by Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 是時關東州、郡務相兼併以自強大，袁紹、袁術亦自相離貳。

translations.literal: At this time the eastern commanderies and districts strove to annex one another to grow strong; Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu also turned against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the east, provinces and commanderies were swallowing one another to grow stronger, and Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu had turned on each other as well.

sentences.zh: 術遣孫堅擊董卓未返，紹以會稽周昂為豫州刺史，襲奪堅陽城。

translations.literal: Shu had sent Sun Jian against Dong Zhuo and he had not returned; Shao installed Zhou Ang of Kuaiji as inspector of Yu province and seized Jian's Yangcheng by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: While Sun Jian was away campaigning against Dong Zhuo, Yuan Shao installed Zhou Ang of Kuaiji as governor of Yu province and seized Sun Jian's base at Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 堅歎曰：「同舉義兵，將救社稷，逆賊垂破而各若此，吾當誰與戮力乎！

translations.literal: Jian sighed and said: "We raised righteous armies together to save altar and state; the traitor is nearly broken—yet each acts like this; with whom shall I exert my strength!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian lamented, "We raised righteous armies together to save the realm. The traitor is nearly broken—yet you turn on one another. With whom am I to fight now?"

sentences.zh: 」引兵擊昂，走之。

translations.literal: " He led troops to attack Ang and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Zhou Ang and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 袁術遣公孫越助堅攻昂，越為流矢所中死。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu sent Gongsun Yue to help Jian attack Ang; Yue was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu sent Gongsun Yue to aid Sun Jian. A stray arrow struck Yue and killed him.

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚怒曰：「余弟死，禍起於紹。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan said in anger: "My younger brother is dead—the calamity arose from Shao."
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan raged, "My brother is dead, and Yuan Shao is to blame."

sentences.zh: 」遂出軍屯磐河，上疏數紹罪惡，進兵攻紹。

translations.literal: " He thereupon marched out and encamped on the Pan River, memorialized enumerating Shao's crimes, and advanced to attack Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to the Pan River, memorialized Yuan Shao's crimes to the court, and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 冀州諸城多畔紹從瓚。

translations.literal: Many cities of Ji province turned from Shao and followed Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Many cities in Ji province defected from Yuan Shao to Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 紹懼，以所佩勃海太守印綬授瓚從弟范，遣之郡，而范遂背紹，領勃海兵以助瓚。

translations.literal: Shao was afraid; he gave the seal and cord of Bohai grand administrator that he wore to Zan's cousin Fan and sent him to the commandery; but Fan then turned against Shao, leading Bohai troops to aid Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Yuan Shao gave his Bohai grand administrator seal to Gongsun Zan's cousin Gongsun Fan and sent him to take the post. Fan promptly betrayed him, mustered Bohai's troops, and joined Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 瓚乃自署其將帥嚴綱為冀州刺史，田楷為青州刺史，單經為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Zan then on his own authority appointed his generals Yan Gang inspector of Ji, Tian Kai inspector of Qing, and Shan Jing inspector of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan then appointed his own men—Yan Gang governor of Ji, Tian Kai governor of Qing, and Shan Jing governor of Yan.

sentences.zh: 又悉改置郡、縣守、令。

translations.literal: He also completely replaced the prefects and magistrates of commanderies and districts.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced commandery and county officials throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 初，涿郡劉備，中山靖王之後也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Bei of Zhuo commandery was a descendant of King Jing of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei of Zhuo commandery was a descendant of Prince Jing of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，與母以販履為業，長七尺五寸，垂手下膝，顧自見其耳；

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he and his mother made a living selling sandals; he stood seven feet five inches; his hands reached his knees; turning his head he could see his own ears;
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he and his mother sold straw sandals for a living. He stood seven feet five inches tall, his hands hung below his knees, and he could see his own ears when he glanced back;

sentences.zh: 有大志，少語言，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: he had great ambition, spoke little, and did not show joy or anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: ambitious, reticent, and never letting joy or anger show on his face.

sentences.zh: 嘗與公孫瓚同師事盧植，由是往依瓚。

translations.literal: He had once studied under Lu Zhi together with Gongsun Zan; for this reason he went to rely on Zan.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under Lu Zhi together with Gongsun Zan and therefore went to serve him.

sentences.zh: 瓚使備與田楷徇青州有功，因以為平原相。

translations.literal: Zan had Bei and Tian Kai campaign in Qing province with merit; he therefore made Bei chancellor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan sent Liu Bei and Tian Kai to campaign in Qing province with success and appointed Bei chancellor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 備少與河東關羽、涿郡張飛相友善；

translations.literal: Bei had been friendly from youth with Guan Yu of Hedong and Zhang Fei of Zhuo commandery;
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liu Bei had been close to Guan Yu of Hedong and Zhang Fei of Zhuo;

sentences.zh: 以羽、飛為別部司馬，分統部曲。

translations.literal: he made Yu and Fei separate-division majors and divided command of the troop detachments.
translations.idiomatic: he made them separate-division majors, each commanding his own troops.

sentences.zh: 備與二人寢則同床，恩若兄弟，而稠人廣坐，侍立終日，隨備周旋，不避艱險。

translations.literal: Bei and the two slept in the same bed; their kindness was like brothers'; yet in crowded halls and broad gatherings they stood in attendance all day, following Bei in his rounds, not shunning hardship or danger.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei shared a bed with them like brothers, yet in company they stood at his side all day, following him through hardship without flinching.

sentences.zh: 常山趙雲為本郡將吏兵詣公孫瓚，瓚曰：「聞貴州人皆願袁氏，君何獨迷而能反乎？

translations.literal: Zhao Yun of Changshan came with the generals, officials, and soldiers of his commandery to Gongsun Zan; Zan said: "I hear all in your noble province wish for the Yuan clan—why alone are you confused and able to turn back?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun of Changshan brought his commandery's troops to Gongsun Zan. Zan said, "Everyone in Changshan favors the Yuans. Why have you alone turned away from them?"

sentences.zh: 」雲曰：「天下訩訩，未知孰是，民有倒縣之厄，鄙州論議，從仁政所在，不為忽袁公，私明將軍也。

translations.literal: " Yun said: "The realm is in uproar; none knows who is right; the people suffer the peril of being hung upside down; in our humble province the discussion is to follow where humane government lies—not to slight Lord Yuan, nor to favor the general in private."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun replied, "The realm is in chaos and no one knows who is right. The people hang by a thread. In Changshan we follow wherever humane government appears—not to slight Lord Yuan, nor out of private favor to you."

sentences.zh: 」劉備見而奇之，深加接納，雲遂從備至平原，為備主騎兵。

translations.literal: " When Liu Bei saw him he marveled at him, received him deeply, and Yun followed Bei to Pingyuan, commanding Bei's cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was impressed and warmly welcomed him. Zhao Yun followed him to Pingyuan and commanded his cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初，袁術之得南陽，戶口數百萬，而術奢淫肆欲，徵斂無度，百姓苦之，稍稍離散。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan Shu took Nanyang, its registered households numbered in the millions; yet Shu was extravagant, lecherous, and unrestrained in desire; his levies were without limit; the hundred surnames suffered; little by little they scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu seized Nanyang it held millions of people, but he was extravagant and rapacious, taxed without limit, and drove the people away in growing numbers.

sentences.zh: 既與袁紹有隙，各立黨援以相圖謀。

translations.literal: Once he had a rift with Yuan Shao, each raised factional allies to plot against the other.
translations.idiomatic: After he broke with Yuan Shao, each rallied allies and schemed against the other.

sentences.zh: 術結公孫瓚而紹連劉表，豪桀多附於紹。

translations.literal: Shu allied with Gongsun Zan while Shao linked with Liu Biao; many powerful men attached to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu allied with Gongsun Zan while Yuan Shao drew Liu Biao; most leading men sided with Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 術怒曰：「群豎不吾從而從吾家奴乎！

translations.literal: Shu said angrily: "Will this pack of nobodies not follow me but follow my family's slave!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu fumed, "Will these nobodies follow me, or my family's bondservant?"

sentences.zh: 」又與公孫瓚書曰：「紹非袁氏子。

translations.literal: " He also wrote to Gongsun Zan: "Shao is not a son of the Yuan clan."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Gongsun Zan, "Yuan Shao is not a true son of the Yuan family."

sentences.zh: 」紹聞大怒。

translations.literal: " When Shao heard he was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao was furious when he heard this.

sentences.zh: 術使孫堅擊劉表，表遣其將黃祖逆戰於樊、鄧之間，堅擊破之，遂圍襄陽。

translations.literal: Shu had Sun Jian attack Liu Biao; Biao sent his general Huang Zu to meet the attack between Fan and Deng; Jian defeated him and thereupon besieged Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu sent Sun Jian against Liu Biao. Liu Biao sent Huang Zu to block him between Fan and Deng. Sun Jian defeated him and besieged Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 表夜遣黃祖潛出發兵，祖將兵欲還，堅逆與戰，祖敗走，竄峴山中。

translations.literal: Biao by night sent Huang Zu out in secret to raise troops; Zu led troops intending to return; Jian met him in counterattack; Zu was defeated and fled, hiding in Mount Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent Huang Zu out by night to gather reinforcements. As Huang Zu marched back, Sun Jian intercepted him, routed him, and drove him into the Xian hills.

sentences.zh: 堅乘勝夜追祖，祖部兵從竹木間暗射堅，殺之。

translations.literal: Jian pressed the victory and pursued Zu by night; Zu's troops shot Jian from ambush among bamboo and trees, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian pursued through the night. Huang Zu's men shot him from the woods and killed him.

sentences.zh: 堅所舉孝廉長沙桓階詣表堅喪，表義而許之。

translations.literal: Huan Jie of Changsha, a filial and incorrupt nominee whom Jian had recommended, came to Biao to attend Jian's mourning; Biao, approving his righteousness, granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jie of Changsha, whom Sun Jian had recommended as a filial nominee, came to Liu Biao to mourn Sun Jian, and Liu Biao, approving his loyalty, allowed it.

sentences.zh: 堅兄子賁率其士眾就袁術，術復表賁為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian's nephew Ben led his soldiers and masses to Yuan Shu; Shu again memorialized that Ben be inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian's nephew Sun Ben led his troops to Yuan Shu, who again recommended him as governor of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 術由是不能勝表。

translations.literal: Shu thereby could not overcome Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu could not defeat Liu Biao after this.

sentences.zh: 初，董卓入關，留朱儁守雒陽，而儁潛與山東諸將通謀，懼為卓所襲，出奔荊州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Dong Zhuo entered the passes, he left Zhu Jun to guard Luoyang; but Jun secretly communicated and plotted with the generals east of the mountains; fearing Zhuo would attack, he fled to Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo entered the passes he left Zhu Jun in Luoyang. Zhu Jun secretly conspired with the eastern warlords and, fearing attack, fled to Jing province.

sentences.zh: 卓以弘農楊懿為河南尹；

translations.literal: Zhuo appointed Yang Yi of Hongnong as Intendant of Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo appointed Yang Yi of Hongnong Intendant of Henan;

sentences.zh: 儁復引兵還雒，擊懿，走之。

translations.literal: Jun again led troops back to Luo, attacked Yi, and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun marched back to Luoyang, attacked Yang Yi, and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 儁以河南殘破無所資，乃東屯中牟，移書州郡，請師討卓。

translations.literal: Jun, because Henan was ruined and offered no resources, then encamped east at Zhongmou, sent letters to provinces and commanderies, and requested troops to attack Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Henan too devastated to supply his army, Zhu Jun encamped at Zhongmou in the east and called on the provinces to send troops against Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史陶謙上儁行車騎將軍，遣精兵三千助之，餘州郡亦有所給。

translations.literal: Tao Qian, inspector of Xu province, memorialized that Jun act as General of Chariots and Cavalry; he sent three thousand picked troops to aid him; other provinces and commanderies also contributed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu province governor Tao Qian petitioned for Zhu Jun to serve as General of Chariots and Cavalry and sent three thousand elite troops; other provinces sent aid as well.

sentences.zh: 謙，丹楊人。

translations.literal: Qian was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian was a native of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以黃巾寇亂徐州，用謙為刺史。

translations.literal: The court, because Yellow Turbans raided and troubled Xu province, employed Qian as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him governor of Xu province when Yellow Turban rebels ravaged the region.

sentences.zh: 謙至，擊黃巾，大破走之，州境晏然。

translations.literal: When Qian arrived, he attacked the Yellow Turbans, crushed them and drove them off, and the province was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived, defeated the Yellow Turbans, and restored peace to the province.

sentences.zh: 劉焉在益州陰圖異計。

translations.literal: Liu Yan in Yi province secretly plotted irregular designs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yi province Liu Yan was secretly pursuing his own designs.

sentences.zh: 沛人張魯，自祖父陵以來世為五斗米道，客居於蜀。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu of Pei, from his grandfather Ling onward for generations practiced the Five Pecks of Rice Way, living as guests in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu of Pei came from a family that for generations had led the Five Pecks of Rice faith, living in exile in Shu.

sentences.zh: 魯母以鬼道常往來焉家，焉乃以魯為督義司馬，以張脩為別部司馬，與合兵掩殺漢中太守蘇固，斷絕斜谷閣，殺害漢使。

translations.literal: Lu's mother by ghost-way often came and went at Yan's house; Yan thereupon made Lu Director of Righteousness Major and Zhang Xiu Separate-Division Major; together they surprised and killed Hanzhong administrator Su Gu, cut off the communications at Xiegu Pass, and killed Han envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu's mother practiced spirit cults and frequented Liu Yan's household. Liu Yan made Zhang Lu Director of Righteousness and Zhang Xiu a separate-division major. Together they ambushed Hanzhong governor Su Gu, sealed the Xiegu Pass, and killed imperial envoys.

sentences.zh: 焉上書言：「米賊斷道，不得復通。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized: "Rice-bandits have cut the road; communication cannot be restored."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan reported to court, "Rice-bandits have cut the roads and traffic cannot get through."

sentences.zh: 」又托他事殺州中豪強王鹹、李權等十餘人，以立威刑。

translations.literal: " He also on pretext of other matters killed more than ten powerful men of the province such as Wang Xian and Li Quan, to establish awe through punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also used other pretexts to execute more than a dozen local magnates, including Wang Xian and Li Quan, to enforce his authority.

sentences.zh: 犍為太守任岐及校尉賈龍由此起兵攻焉，焉擊殺岐、龍。

translations.literal: Ren Qi, grand administrator of Jianwei, and Commandant Jia Long thereupon raised troops to attack Yan; Yan attacked and killed Qi and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwei governor Ren Qi and Commandant Jia Long rose against him; Liu Yan defeated and killed them both.

sentences.zh: 焉意漸盛，作乘輿車具千餘乘，劉表上「焉有似子夏在西河疑聖人」之論。

translations.literal: Yan's intentions grew increasingly proud; he made more than a thousand sets of imperial carriage fittings; Liu Biao memorialized the opinion that "Yan resembles Zixia at Xihe doubting the sage."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan grew bolder, had more than a thousand imperial chariots built, and Liu Biao memorialized that he was like Zixia of Xihe doubting a sage—implying sedition.

sentences.zh: 時焉子范為左中郎將，誕為治書御史，璋為奉車都尉，皆從帝在長安，惟小子別部車馬瑁素隨焉；

translations.literal: At that time Yan's sons Fan was Left Central Gentleman, Dan was Master of Writing Censor, and Zhang was Chief Commandant of the Imperial Carriages—all followed the emperor in Chang'an; only his youngest son, Separate Division Carriages and Horses Mao, had always accompanied Yan;
translations.idiomatic: His sons Fan, Dan, and Zhang held court posts in Chang'an with the emperor; only his youngest son Liu Mao remained with him in Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝使璋曉喻焉，焉留璋不遣。

translations.literal: the emperor sent Zhang to enlighten and instruct Yan; Yan detained Zhang and would not send him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Liu Zhang to reason with his father, but Liu Yan kept him there.

sentences.zh: 公孫度威行海外，中國人士避亂者多歸之，北海管寧、邴原、王烈皆往依焉。

translations.literal: Gongsun Du's authority reached beyond the seas; many persons of the central states fleeing turmoil came to him; Guan Ning, Bing Yuan, and Wang Lie of Beihai all went to rely on Du.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du's authority extended overseas, and many refugees from the heartland joined him, including Guan Ning, Bing Yuan, and Wang Lie of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 寧少時與華歆為友，嘗與歆共鋤菜，見地有金，寧揮鋤不顧，與瓦石無異，歆捉而擲之，人以是知其優劣。

translations.literal: Ning in youth was friends with Hua Xin; once hoeing vegetables together with Xin they saw gold in the ground; Ning waved his hoe and did not look—it was no different from tile or stone; Xin picked it up and threw it away; people thereby knew their superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning had been friends with Hua Xin since youth. Once while hoeing together they found gold. Guan Ning ignored it as if it were rubble; Hua Xin picked it up, then tossed it away. Onlookers took this as measure of their character.

sentences.zh: 邴原遠行遊學，八九年而歸，師友以原不飲酒，會米肉送之，原曰：「本能飲酒，但以荒思廢業，故斷之耳。

translations.literal: Bing Yuan traveled far to study; after eight or nine years he returned; teachers and friends, because Yuan did not drink wine, gathered rice and meat to send him off; Yuan said: "By nature I could drink, but because dissipation of thought would ruin my studies, I cut it off."
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan studied abroad for eight or nine years. When he returned, his teachers and friends—knowing he abstained from wine—gathered a farewell feast with rice and meat. Bing Yuan said, "I can drink, but I gave it up lest dissipation ruin my studies."

sentences.zh: 今當遠別，可一飲燕。

translations.literal: Now we are to part far; we may drink once in convivial farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we part for long, let us share one cup.

sentences.zh: 」於是共坐飲酒，終日不醉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they sat together and drank; all day they did not become drunk.
translations.idiomatic: They drank together all day and Bing Yuan never became drunk.

sentences.zh: 寧、原俱以操尚稱，度虛館以候之。

translations.literal: Ning and Yuan both were famed for lofty conduct; Du prepared empty lodges to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Both were famed for upright character, and Gongsun Du prepared lodgings to receive them.

sentences.zh: 寧既見度，乃廬於山谷。

translations.literal: When Ning had seen Du, he then built a hut in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: After meeting Gongsun Du, Guan Ning built a cottage in the hills.

sentences.zh: 時避難者多居郡南，而寧獨居北，示無還志，後漸來從之，旬月而成邑。

translations.literal: At the time many refugees dwelt in the south of the commandery, but Ning alone dwelt in the north, showing he had no mind to return; later people gradually came to follow him; in a month or so it became a settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees clustered in the south of the commandery, but Guan Ning settled alone in the north to show he would not stay. Others gradually joined him, and within a month a community had formed.

sentences.zh: 寧每見度，語唯經典，不及世事；

translations.literal: Whenever Ning saw Du, his speech was only of the classics, not reaching to affairs of the age;
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Ning met Gongsun Du he spoke only of the classics, never of worldly affairs;

sentences.zh: 還山，專講《詩》、《書》，習俎豆，非學者無見也。

translations.literal: returning to the hills he lectured exclusively on the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, practiced sacrificial vessels; those who were not scholars he did not see.
translations.idiomatic: and back in the hills he taught the Odes and Documents, trained students in ritual, and admitted no one but scholars.

sentences.zh: 由是度安其賢，民化其德。

translations.literal: From this Du was reassured by his worth; the people were transformed by his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du trusted in his integrity, and the people were moved by his example.

sentences.zh: 邴原性剛直，清議以格物，度已下心不安之。

translations.literal: Bing Yuan's nature was obstinate and upright; pure discourse to correct things—Du inwardly was ill at ease because of him.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan was blunt and quick to moralize. Gongsun Du grew uneasy under his scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 寧謂原曰：「潛龍以不見成德。

translations.literal: Ning said to Yuan: "The hidden dragon completes his virtue by not being seen."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning told Bing Yuan, "The hidden dragon perfects his virtue by staying unseen."

sentences.zh: 言非其時，皆招禍之道也。

translations.literal: Words not at their proper time are all roads that invite calamity.
translations.idiomatic: To speak out of season is to invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 」密遣原逃歸，度聞之，亦不復追也。

translations.literal: [He] secretly sent Yuan to flee home; when Du heard of it, he did not pursue him again.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent Yuan back to escape; when Gongsun Du learned of it, he made no further attempt to pursue him.

sentences.zh: 王烈器業過人，少時名聞在原、寧之右。

translations.literal: Wang Lie's capacity and achievement surpassed others; in youth his fame was heard to the right of Yuan and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lie's talent and conduct surpassed those of his peers; in his youth his reputation even eclipsed that of Yuan and Ning.

sentences.zh: 善於教誘，鄉里有盜牛者，主得之，盜請罪，曰：「刑戮是甘，乞不使王彥方知也！

translations.literal: He was skilled at teaching and guiding. In the district there was one who stole an ox; the owner caught him. The thief pleaded guilty, saying: "Punishment by law I gladly accept—I beg only that Lord Wang Yanfang not be told!"
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at instruction and moral guidance. When a man in his district stole an ox and was caught by the owner, the thief confessed and said, "I will gladly accept legal punishment—only I beg that Lord Wang Yanfang never learn of this!"

sentences.zh: 」烈聞而使人謝之，遺布一端。

translations.literal: When Lie heard, he sent someone to thank him and gave a bolt of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Lie heard of this, he sent someone to thank the man and gave him a bolt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，烈曰：「盜懼吾聞其過，是有恥惡之心，既知恥惡，則善心將生，故與布以勸為善也。

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason. Lie said: "The thief feared that I would hear of his fault—this is having a mind ashamed of evil. Once he knows shame of evil, a good heart will be born; therefore I gave cloth to encourage doing good."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Lie said, "The thief feared that I would learn of his crime—that shows he still felt shame at wrongdoing. Once a man knows shame, a good heart will grow in him; so I gave him cloth to encourage him toward virtue."

sentences.zh: 」後有老父遺劍於路，行道一人見而守之。

translations.literal: Later an old man left a sword on the road; a man on the road who saw it guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: Later an old man dropped a sword on the road; a passerby who saw it stood watch over it.

sentences.zh: 至暮，老父還，尋得劍，怪之，以事告烈，烈使推求，乃先盜牛者也。

translations.literal: By evening the old man returned, sought and found the sword, and marveled. He told Lie of the affair; Lie had it traced, and it was the same man who had earlier stolen the ox.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the old man came back, found his sword, and was astonished. He told Lie what had happened; Lie had the matter investigated, and the guardian proved to be the same man who had once stolen the ox.

sentences.zh: 諸有爭訟曲直將質之於烈，或至塗而反，或望廬而還，皆相推以直，不敢使烈聞之。

translations.literal: All who had lawsuits about right and wrong would have brought them to Lie for judgment; some turned back halfway on the road, some returned on sight of his house—all pushed one another to yield what was right, not daring to let Lie hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever neighbors had disputes they meant to bring before Lie for judgment, some would turn back halfway along the road, others would go home at the mere sight of his dwelling—all yielding to one another rather than pressing their claims, for fear that Lie might hear of their quarrel.

sentences.zh: 度欲以為長史，烈辭之，為商賈以自穢，乃免。

translations.literal: Du wished to make him Chief Clerk; Lie declined, became a merchant to defile himself, and was thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du wanted to appoint him Chief Clerk, but Lie refused; he took up trade as a merchant to degrade himself in Du's eyes, and so escaped the appointment.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁丑，赦天下。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day dingchou—amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the dingchou day of the first month, an empire-wide amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 董卓遣牛輔將兵屯陝，輔分遣校尉北地李傕、張掖郭汜、武威張濟將步騎數萬擊破朱儁於中牟，因掠陳留、穎川諸縣，所過殺虜無遺。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo sent Niu Fu to lead troops and encamp at Shaan. Fu detached Commandants Li Jue of Beidi, Guo Si of Zhangye, and Zhang Ji of Wuwei with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry, who defeated Zhu Jun at Zhongmou and then plundered the counties of Chenliu and Yingchuan, killing and carrying off all they passed, leaving none.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sent Niu Fu to garrison Shaan with an army; Fu in turn detached the commandants Li Jue of Beidi, Guo Si of Zhangye, and Zhang Ji of Wuwei, who led tens of thousands of foot and horse soldiers to crush Zhu Jun at Zhongmou, then swept through Chenliu and Yingchuan, slaughtering and plundering every place they touched until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 初，荀淑有孫曰彧，少有才名，何顒見而異之，曰：「王佐才也！

translations.literal: Earlier, Xun Shu had a grandson named Yu, who in youth had talent and fame. He Yong saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, saying: "Talent fit to assist a king!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xun Shu had a grandson named Yu who won early renown for his ability. When He Yong met him, he was struck with wonder and declared, "Here is a man born to serve at a ruler's right hand!"

sentences.zh: 」及天下亂，彧謂父老曰：「穎川四戰之地，宜亟避之。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into disorder, Yu said to the elders of his district: "Yingchuan is a place of four-sided warfare—we should flee it at once."
translations.idiomatic: When the empire plunged into chaos, Yu told the elders of his home district, "Yingchuan lies where armies from every direction will collide—you must leave at once."

sentences.zh: 」鄉人多懷土不能去，彧獨率宗族去依韓馥。

translations.literal: Many of the villagers clung to their land and could not leave; Yu alone led his clan to rely on Han Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his neighbors could not bear to abandon their homes, but Yu alone led his clan away to take refuge with Han Fu.

sentences.zh: 會袁紹已奪馥位，待彧以上賓之禮。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuan Shao had already seized Fu's position and treated Yu with the courtesy due a chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuan Shao had already displaced Han Fu and received Yu with the honors reserved for a most honored guest.

sentences.zh: 彧度紹終不能定大業，聞曹操有雄略，乃去紹從操。

translations.literal: Yu judged that Shao in the end could not settle the great enterprise; hearing that Cao Cao had heroic strategy, he left Shao and followed Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu judged that Yuan Shao would never secure the empire; hearing that Cao Cao possessed true strategic vision, he left Shao and entered Cao's service.

sentences.zh: 操與語，大悅，曰：「吾子房也！

translations.literal: Cao spoke with him and was greatly pleased, saying: "You are my Zifang!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao talked with him and was delighted, exclaiming, "You are my Zhang Liang!"

sentences.zh: 」以為奮武司馬。

translations.literal: He was made Martial-Exertion Major.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yu Martial-Exertion Major.

sentences.zh: 其鄉人留者，多為傕、汜等所殺。

translations.literal: Those of his fellow villagers who remained were mostly killed by Li Jue, Guo Si, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the neighbors who had stayed behind were slaughtered by Li Jue, Guo Si, and their bands.

sentences.zh: 袁紹自出拒公孫瓚，與瓚戰於界橋南二十里。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao himself went out to resist Gongsun Zan and fought Zan twenty li south of Jie Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao marched out in person to oppose Gongsun Zan and met him in battle twenty li south of Jie Bridge.

sentences.zh: 瓚兵三萬，其鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: Zan's troops numbered thirty thousand, and their spearhead was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Zan fielded thirty thousand men, and their vanguard was fierce.

sentences.zh: 紹令麴義領精兵八百先登，強弩千張夾承之。

translations.literal: Shao ordered Qu Yi to lead eight hundred picked troops to ascend first; a thousand strong crossbows flanked and supported them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao ordered Qu Yi to lead eight hundred elite soldiers forward in the van, with a thousand powerful crossbows arrayed on either flank to support them.

sentences.zh: 瓚輕其兵少，縱騎騰之。

translations.literal: Zan despised their few troops and loosed his cavalry to charge them.
translations.idiomatic: Zan scorned their small numbers and sent his horsemen charging down upon them.

sentences.zh: 義兵伏楯下不動，未至十數步，一時同發，歡呼動地，瓚軍大敗。

translations.literal: Yi's troops lay behind their shields without moving; before ten-odd paces were reached, all fired at once. Their shouts shook the earth, and Zan's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's men crouched motionless behind their shields; when the enemy drew within a dozen paces, every crossbow let fly at once. Their battle cry shook the ground, and Zan's army collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 斬其所置冀州刺史嚴綱，獲甲首千餘級。

translations.literal: They beheaded Yan Gang, whom he had installed as Inspector of Ji Province, and took more than a thousand armored heads.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Yan Gang, whom Zan had appointed Inspector of Ji Province, and took more than a thousand armored heads as trophies.

sentences.zh: 追至界橋，瓚斂兵還戰，義復破之，遂到瓚營，拔其牙門，餘眾皆走。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Jie Bridge, Zan gathered his troops and turned to fight again; Yi again defeated him, then reached Zan's camp, tore down his command gate, and the rest all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit carried them to Jie Bridge, where Zan rallied his forces for another stand; Yi broke them again, pressed on to Zan's camp, tore down his command gate, and the remainder of his army scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 初，兗州刺史劉岱與紹、瓚連和，紹令妻子居岱所，瓚亦遣從事范方將騎助岱。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Dai, Inspector of Yan Province, was allied with both Shao and Zan. Shao had his wife and children dwell at Dai's place; Zan also sent his attendant Fan Fang to lead cavalry to aid Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Dai, Inspector of Yan Province, had been on friendly terms with both Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan. Shao had lodged his wife and children with Dai, while Zan too had sent his aide Fan Fang at the head of a cavalry detachment to support him.

sentences.zh: 及瓚擊破紹軍，語岱令遣紹妻子，別敕范方：「若岱不遣紹家，將騎還！

translations.literal: When Zan had defeated Shao's army, he told Dai to send away Shao's wife and children, and separately ordered Fan Fang: "If Dai does not send away Shao's family, lead the cavalry back!"
translations.idiomatic: After Zan routed Yuan Shao's forces, he ordered Dai to send Shao's family away and separately instructed Fan Fang, "If Dai refuses to expel Shao's household, march your horsemen home at once!"

sentences.zh: 吾定紹，將加兵於岱。

translations.literal: When I have settled Shao, I will turn my troops upon Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Once I have finished with Shao, I will bring my army down on Dai as well.

sentences.zh: 」岱與官屬議，連日不決，聞東郡程昱有智謀，召而問之，昱曰：「若棄紹近援而求瓚遠助，此假人於越以救溺子之說也。

translations.literal: Dai discussed with his officials for days without deciding. Hearing that Cheng Yu of Dong Commandery had wisdom and stratagems, he summoned and questioned him. Yu said: "If you abandon Shao's nearby aid and seek Zan's distant help, this is the notion of borrowing a man from Yue to save a drowning son."
translations.idiomatic: Dai debated the matter with his staff for days without reaching a decision. Hearing that Cheng Yu of Dong Commandery was a man of keen counsel, he summoned him and asked his view. Yu said, "To cast off Yuan Shao's aid close at hand and court Gongsun Zan's help from afar is like hiring a man from distant Yue to rescue your drowning child."

sentences.zh: 夫公孫瓚非袁紹之敵也，今雖壞紹軍，然終為紹所禽。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan is no match for Yuan Shao; though he has now broken Shao's army, in the end he will be captured by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan is no match for Yuan Shao. He may have shattered Shao's army today, but in the end Shao will be the one who destroys him.

sentences.zh: 」岱從之。

translations.literal: Dai followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Dai took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 范方將其騎歸，未至而瓚敗。

translations.literal: Fan Fang led his cavalry back; before he arrived, Zan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Fang marched his horsemen homeward, but before he could arrive, Zan had already been defeated.

sentences.zh: 曹操軍頓丘，於毒等攻東武陽。

translations.literal: Cao Cao's army was at Dunqiu; Yu Du and others attacked Dongwuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's army was encamped at Dunqiu when Yu Du and his band laid siege to Dongwuyang.

sentences.zh: 操引兵西入山，攻毒等本屯。

translations.literal: Cao led his troops west into the mountains to attack Yu Du and the others' base camp.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched west into the hills to strike at the rebels' base camp.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆請救武陽。

translations.literal: All the generals asked to relieve Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: His officers all urged him to march to the relief of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 操曰：「使賊聞我西而還，武陽自解也，不過，我能敗其本屯；

translations.literal: Cao said: "If the bandits hear that I have gone west and return, Wuyang will relieve itself of itself. Even if they do not, I can defeat their base camp."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Once the rebels hear that I have marched west, they will abandon the siege and Wuyang will save itself. And even if they do not, I can still crush their base camp."

sentences.zh: 虜不能拔武陽必矣。

translations.literal: The enemy certainly cannot take Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: They will certainly never be able to take Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 」遂行。

translations.literal: He thereupon marched.
translations.idiomatic: With that he pressed on westward.

sentences.zh: 毒聞之，棄武陽還。

translations.literal: When Yu Du heard, he abandoned Wuyang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Du heard of Cao's move, he broke off the siege and marched back.

sentences.zh: 操遂擊眭固及匈奴於夫羅於內黃，皆大破之。

translations.literal: Cao then attacked Sui Gu and the Xiongnu Yufuluo at Neihuang and utterly defeated them both.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then struck Sui Gu and the Xiongnu chieftain Yufuluo at Neihuang and routed them both.

sentences.zh: 董卓以其弟旻為左將軍，兄子璜為中軍校尉，皆典兵事，宗族內外並列朝廷。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo made his younger brother Min Left General and his elder brother's son Huang Central Army Commandant; both held military affairs, and his clan inside and outside all stood in ranks at court.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo appointed his younger brother Min Left General and his nephew Huang Central Army Commandant; both controlled military affairs, while his kinsmen, near and remote, packed the offices of the court.

sentences.zh: 卓侍妾懷抱中子皆封侯，弄以金紫。

translations.literal: Zhuo's concubines and the sons in their arms were all enfeoffed as marquises, dandled in gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhuo's concubines and the infants they nursed were enfeoffed as marquises, paraded about in gold seals and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 卓車服僭擬天子，召呼三台，尚書以下皆自詣卓府啟事。
