translations.literal: Zhuo's carriage and dress usurped and imitated the Son of Heaven; he summoned and called the Three Excellencies, and all from Masters of Writing down went in person to Zhuo's mansion to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's carriage and regalia aped those of the emperor; he summoned the Three Excellencies at will, and every official from the Masters of Writing downward had to report in person at Zhuo's mansion.

sentences.zh: 又築塢於郿，高厚皆七丈，積穀為三十年儲，自云：「事成，雄據天下；

translations.literal: He also built a fortified village at Mei, seven zhang in height and thickness, and stored grain for thirty years' supply. He himself said: "If the enterprise succeeds, I will hold the realm in heroic dominance;"
translations.idiomatic: He also built a fortified stronghold at Mei, seven zhang high and thick, and stocked it with grain enough for thirty years. He declared, "If my plans succeed, I shall rule the empire in might;"

sentences.zh: 不成，守此足以畢老。

translations.literal: "if it does not succeed, holding this is enough to finish my old age."
translations.idiomatic: "if they fail, holding this place will be enough to see out my days."

sentences.zh: 」卓忍於誅殺，諸將言語有蹉跌者，便戮於前，人不聊生。

translations.literal: Zhuo was ruthless in executions; if any general's words had a slip or stumble, he was killed on the spot before him. People had no livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was merciless with the sword: if a general's words so much as stumbled, the man was cut down before his eyes. The people could barely endure life.

sentences.zh: 司徒王允與司隸校尉黃琬、僕射士孫瑞、尚書楊瓚密謀誅卓。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Wang Yun, with Director of the Imperial Secretariat Huang Wan, Deputy Director Shi Sun Rui, and Master of Writing Yang Zan, secretly plotted to kill Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister over the Masses Wang Yun joined the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Huang Wan, the Deputy Director Shi Sun Rui, and the Master of Writing Yang Zan in a secret plot to kill Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 中郎將呂布，便弓馬，膂力過人，卓自以遇人無禮，行止常以布自衛，甚愛信之，誓為父子。

translations.literal: General of the Gentlemen of the Household Lü Bu was skilled with bow and horse, his bodily strength surpassing others. Zhuo, knowing himself rude in meeting people, constantly used Bu to guard himself in going and stopping, loved and trusted him greatly, and swore to be father and son.
translations.idiomatic: The General of the Gentlemen of the Household Lü Bu was a master of bow and saddle and possessed strength beyond ordinary men. Zhuo, knowing how roughly he treated others, kept Bu at his side wherever he went, cherished and trusted him deeply, and bound him with an oath of father and son.

sentences.zh: 然卓性剛褊，嘗小失卓意，卓拔手戟擲布，布拳捷避之，而改容顧謝，卓意亦解。

translations.literal: Yet Zhuo's nature was harsh and narrow. Once when he slightly missed Zhuo's intent, Zhuo drew his hand halberd and hurled it at Bu. Bu, agile with his fists, dodged it, then changed his expression and turned to apologize, and Zhuo's mind also eased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhuo was harsh and quick to take offense. Once, when Bu had slightly displeased him, Zhuo snatched up a hand halberd and hurled it at him. Bu, quick as a boxer, dodged aside, then composed his face and apologized, and Zhuo's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 布由是陰怨於卓。

translations.literal: From this Bu secretly resented Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment Bu nursed a secret grudge against Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓又使布守中閣，而私於傅婢，益不自安。

translations.literal: Zhuo also had Bu guard the inner gate, while he privately took liberties with a maid of Bu's household, and Bu grew still more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo also set Bu to guard the inner apartments, yet took Bu's maid as his lover on the side, which left Bu more uneasy than ever.

sentences.zh: 王允素善待布，布見允，自陳卓幾見殺之狀，允因以誅卓之謀告布，使為內應。

translations.literal: Wang Yun had always treated Bu well. Bu saw Yun and himself described how Zhuo had nearly killed him. Yun thereupon told Bu the plan to kill Zhuo and had him act as inner accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun had long treated Bu with kindness. When Bu came to him and described how Zhuo had nearly killed him, Yun revealed the plot against Zhuo and enlisted him as the man within.

sentences.zh: 布曰：「如父子何？

translations.literal: Bu said: "What of the father-and-son bond?"
translations.idiomatic: Bu said, "But what of our bond as father and son?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「君自姓呂，本非骨肉。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Your surname is Lü by nature—you are not flesh and bone to begin with."
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "Your name is Lü—you were never his kin by blood."

sentences.zh: 今憂死不暇，何謂父子？

translations.literal: Now you worry that you have no leisure from death—what talk of father and son?
translations.idiomatic: You fret now only that you may not escape death—what father-and-son bond can that be?

sentences.zh: 擲戟之時，豈有父子情邪！

translations.literal: When he hurled the halberd, was there any father-and-son feeling?
translations.idiomatic: When he hurled that halberd at you, did that look like a father's love?

sentences.zh: 」布遂許之。

translations.literal: Bu thereupon agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bu agreed at last.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁巳，帝有疾新愈，大會未央殿。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day dingsi—the Emperor's illness had newly healed, and a great assembly was held in Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the dingsi day of the fourth month, the emperor, newly recovered from illness, held a great court assembly in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 卓朝服乘車而入，陳兵夾道，自營至宮，左步右騎，屯衛周匝，令呂布等扞衛前後。

translations.literal: Zhuo entered in court dress riding in a carriage, with troops arrayed along the road from his camp to the palace—infantry on the left, cavalry on the right, garrisons encircling all around—and ordered Lü Bu and others to guard before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo entered in full court dress, riding in his carriage, with soldiers lining the road from his camp to the palace—foot soldiers on the left, horsemen on the right, pickets posted all around—and ordered Lü Bu and the rest to guard him fore and aft.

sentences.zh: 王允使士孫瑞自書詔以授布，布令同郡騎都尉李肅與勇士秦誼、陳衛等十餘人偽著衛士服，守北掖門內以待卓。

translations.literal: Wang Yun had Shi Sun Rui write the edict himself and give it to Bu. Bu ordered his fellow townsman Commandant of Cavalry Li Su, with the warriors Qin Yi, Chen Wei, and more than ten others, to don guards' dress falsely and wait inside the North Side Gate for Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun had Shi Sun Rui draft the imperial order in his own hand and pass it to Bu. Bu then ordered his fellow townsman, the Commandant of Cavalry Li Su, together with the warriors Qin Yi, Chen Wei, and a dozen more, to disguise themselves as palace guards and wait inside the North Side Gate for Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓入門，肅以戟刺之；

translations.literal: When Zhuo entered the gate, Su stabbed him with a halberd;
translations.idiomatic: As Zhuo passed through the gate, Li Su struck him with a halberd;

sentences.zh: 卓衷甲，不入，傷臂，墮車，顧大呼曰：「呂布何在？

translations.literal: Zhuo wore armor beneath; it did not pierce through. His arm was wounded, he fell from the carriage, turned his head and shouted loudly: "Where is Lü Bu?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo wore armor beneath his robes, so the blow did not pierce deep, but his arm was wounded and he tumbled from his carriage. He turned and bellowed, "Where is Lü Bu?"

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「有詔討賊臣！

translations.literal: Bu said: "There is an edict to punish the traitor minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Bu answered, "By imperial order—death to the traitor!"

sentences.zh: 」卓大罵曰：「庸狗，敢如是邪！

translations.literal: Zhuo cursed loudly: "Worthless cur—dare you act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo raged, "Worthless cur—how dare you!"

sentences.zh: 」布應聲持矛刺卓，趣兵斬之。

translations.literal: Bu, answering to the sound, took a spear and stabbed Zhuo, urging the soldiers to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Bu answered with a thrust of his spear and ordered the soldiers to cut Zhuo down.

sentences.zh: 主簿田儀及卓倉頭前赴其屍，布又殺之，凡所殺三人。

translations.literal: Registrar Tian Yi and Zhuo's steward rushed forward to his corpse; Bu killed them too—in all three were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar Tian Yi and Zhuo's steward rushed to his body; Bu killed them as well, three men in all.

sentences.zh: 布即出懷中詔版以令吏士曰：「詔討卓耳，餘皆不問。

translations.literal: Bu at once produced the edict tablet from his bosom and ordered the clerks and soldiers, saying: "The edict punishes Zhuo only; the rest are not to be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Bu at once produced the edict tablet from his robe and proclaimed to the officials and troops, "The order was to punish Zhuo alone; no one else is to be harmed."

sentences.zh: 」吏士皆正立不動，大稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The clerks and soldiers all stood upright without moving and shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The officials and soldiers stood motionless in their ranks and shouted, "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 百姓歌舞於道，長安中士女賣其珠玉衣裝市酒肉相慶者，填滿街肆。

translations.literal: The common people sang and danced in the roads; in Chang'an gentlemen and women sold their pearls, jade, and dress to buy wine and meat in celebration, filling the streets and markets.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners sang and danced in the streets, while throughout Chang'an men and women sold pearls, jade, and finery to buy wine and meat for celebration until the markets overflowed.

sentences.zh: 弟旻、璜等及宗族老弱在郿，皆為其群下所斫射死。

translations.literal: His younger brother Min, Huang, and the like, with the old and weak of the clan at Mei, were all hacked and shot to death by Zhuo's subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Min, his nephew Huang, and the rest of the clan—the aged and the helpless alike—at the Mei stronghold were all cut down and shot dead by Zhuo's own followers.

sentences.zh: 暴卓屍於市。

translations.literal: Zhuo's corpse was exposed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's corpse was displayed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 天時始熱，卓素充肥，脂流於地，守屍吏為大炷，置卓臍中然之，光明達曙，如是積日。

translations.literal: The season had begun to grow hot; Zhuo had always been full and fat, and grease flowed upon the ground. The corpse-guarding clerks made a great wick, placed it in Zhuo's navel and lit it; the light reached until dawn, and so for many days.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was turning warm; Zhuo had always been grossly obese, and grease pooled on the ground. The guards lit a great wick in his navel; it burned until dawn and did so for days on end.

sentences.zh: 諸袁門生聚董氏之屍，焚灰揚之於路。

translations.literal: The Yuan clansmen's students gathered the Dong clan's corpses, burned them to ash, and scattered the ash upon the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Yuan faction gathered the bodies of the Dong clan, burned them to ash, and scattered the ashes along the roads.

sentences.zh: 塢中有金二三萬斤，銀八九萬斤，錦綺奇玩積如丘山。

translations.literal: In the fortified village there were twenty or thirty thousand jin of gold, eighty or ninety thousand jin of silver, and brocades, silks, and rare curios piled like hills.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the stronghold were twenty or thirty thousand jin of gold, eighty or ninety thousand jin of silver, and brocades, silks, and curios heaped like hills.

sentences.zh: 以王允錄尚書事，呂布為奮威將軍、假節、儀比三司，封溫侯，共秉朝政。

translations.literal: Wang Yun was made Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; Lü Bu was made Martial-Exertion General, with provisional staff and ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wen—they together held court government.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun was appointed to record the affairs of the Masters of Writing; Lü Bu was made Martial-Exertion General, granted the ceremonial staff of authority and precedence equal to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wen. Together they held the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 卓之死也，左中郎將高陽侯蔡邕在王允坐，聞之驚歎。

translations.literal: At Zhuo's death, the Left General of the Gentlemen of the Household, Marquis of Gaoyang, Cai Yong, was seated with Wang Yun; hearing of it he started and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo died, the Left General of the Gentlemen of the Household, Marquis of Gaoyang, Cai Yong, was in Wang Yun's company; on hearing the news he gasped and sighed.

sentences.zh: 允勃然叱之曰：「董卓，國之大賊！

translations.literal: Yun flushed with anger and rebuked him, saying: "Dong Zhuo is the great villain of the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Yun flushed with anger and rebuked him: "Dong Zhuo was the empire's greatest villain!"

sentences.zh: 幾亡漢室。

translations.literal: He nearly destroyed the House of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He nearly brought the House of Han to ruin.

sentences.zh: 君為王臣，所宜同疾，而懷其私遇，反相傷痛，豈不共為逆哉！

translations.literal: You are the king's minister and ought to share the same hatred, yet you cherish his private favor toward you and instead show mutual grief—is this not joining in treason together?
translations.idiomatic: You are the emperor's servant and should share our hatred, yet you nurse private gratitude for his favors and grieve his death—are you not his accomplice?

sentences.zh: 」即收付廷尉。

translations.literal: He was at once seized and handed over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had him seized at once and handed over to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 邕謝曰：「身雖不忠，古今大義，耳所厭聞，口所常玩，豈當背國而向卓也！

translations.literal: Yong apologized, saying: "Though my person was not loyal, the great principles of past and present—what the ear loathes to hear and the mouth constantly recites—how could I turn my back on the state and face toward Zhuo!"
translations.idiomatic: Yong pleaded, "I may have failed in loyalty, but the great principles of past and present—the very truths my ears have always shunned in shame and my lips have always rehearsed—how could I ever have turned against the state to serve Zhuo?"

sentences.zh: 願黥首刖足，繼成漢史。

translations.literal: I wish to be tattooed on the head and have my feet cut off, to continue and complete the Han histories.
translations.idiomatic: Let me be branded and maimed if only I may be allowed to finish the history of Han."

sentences.zh: 」士大夫多矜救之，不能得。

translations.literal: Many scholar-officials pitied him and sought to save him, but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Many scholar-officials pleaded for his life, but in vain.

sentences.zh: 太尉馬日磾謂允曰：「伯喈曠世逸才，多識漢事，當續成後史，為一代大典；

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Ma Midi said to Yun: "Bocai is a transcendent talent of an age, deeply versed in Han affairs; he ought to continue and complete the later histories as a great canon of a generation;"
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant Ma Midi said to Yun, "Cai Yong is a talent unmatched in his age, steeped in the affairs of Han. He should be allowed to complete the later histories—a work that would stand as the great record of our time;"

sentences.zh: 而所坐至微。

translations.literal: yet the offense for which he sits is extremely slight.
translations.idiomatic: yet the crime charged against him is trifling.

sentences.zh: 誅之，無乃失人望乎！

translations.literal: To execute him—will you not lose people's hopes?
translations.idiomatic: To put him to death—will you not forfeit the people's regard?"

sentences.zh: 」允曰：「昔武帝不殺司馬遷，使作謗書流於後世。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Formerly Emperor Wu did not kill Sima Qian, and let him compose a book of slander that flowed to later ages."
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "Long ago Emperor Wu spared Sima Qian's life, and the man left behind a history that slandered the throne for generations to come."

sentences.zh: 方今國祚中衰，戎馬在郊，不可令佞臣執筆在幼主左右，既無益聖德，復使吾黨蒙其訕議。

translations.literal: Now the state's fortune is in mid-decline and war-horses are at the suburbs; one cannot let a flatterer hold the brush at the young lord's side—this neither benefits sagely virtue nor keeps our faction from suffering his ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Today the dynasty is in decline and war-horses crowd the suburbs. We cannot let a sycophant hold the brush beside a child emperor—it would do the throne no good, and our party would only suffer his mockery in the histories he wrote."

sentences.zh: 」日磾退而告人曰：「王公其無後乎！

translations.literal: Midi withdrew and told others: "Lord Wang will have no posterity!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Midi withdrew and said to others, "Lord Wang will leave no descendants!"

sentences.zh: 善人，國之紀也；

translations.literal: Good men are the cords of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Good men are the cords that bind a state;

sentences.zh: 製作，國之典也；

translations.literal: composition and creation are the canons of the state;
translations.idiomatic: and written works are its canonical records;

sentences.zh: 滅紀廢典，其能久乎！

translations.literal: to extinguish the cords and abolish the canons—can it long endure?
translations.idiomatic: destroy the one and discard the other—how long can such a regime endure?"

sentences.zh: 」邕遂死獄中。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong died in prison.

sentences.zh: 初，黃門侍郎荀攸與尚書鄭泰、侍中種輯等謀曰：「董卓驕忍無親，雖資強兵，實一匹夫耳，可直刺殺也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yellow Gate Attendant Xun You, with Master of Writing Zheng Tai, Palace Attendant Zhong Yi, and others plotted, saying: "Dong Zhuo is arrogant, cruel, and without kin; though he relies on strong troops, he is in truth but a common fellow—one can stab and kill him outright."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Yellow Gate Attendant Xun You had joined the Master of Writing Zheng Tai, the Palace Attendant Zhong Yi, and others in a plot. They said, "Dong Zhuo is arrogant, cruel, and trusts no one. Though he commands a great army, he is only a common ruffian at heart—he can be struck down with a single thrust."

sentences.zh: 」事垂就而覺，收攸繫獄，泰逃奔袁術。

translations.literal: The affair was on the verge of success when it was discovered; You was seized and imprisoned, Tai fled to Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was nearly carried out when it was discovered. You was arrested and thrown into prison; Tai fled to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 攸言語飲食自若，會卓死。

translations.literal: You's speech and eating and drinking were as if at ease; it happened that Zhuo died.
translations.idiomatic: You ate and spoke as calmly as ever in his cell—then Zhuo died.

sentences.zh: 得免。

translations.literal: He was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He was released.

sentences.zh: 青州黃巾寇兗州，劉岱欲擊之，濟北相鮑信諫曰：「今賊眾百萬，百姓皆震恐，士卒無鬥志，不可敵也。

translations.literal: Qing Province Yellow Turbans raided Yan Province. Liu Dai wished to attack them. Bao Xin, Chancellor of Jibei, remonstrated, saying: "Now the bandits number a million; the common people are all shaken with fear, and the soldiers have no fighting will—they cannot be opposed."
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Turban rebels from Qing Province raided Yan Province. Liu Dai wanted to give battle, but Bao Xin, Chancellor of Jibei, urged against it: "The rebels now number in the millions, the people are terrified, and our troops lack the will to fight. We cannot face them in open battle."

sentences.zh: 然賊軍無輜重，唯以鈔略為資。

translations.literal: Yet the bandit army has no baggage train and relies only on plunder for sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they carry no baggage train and live only by raiding and plunder."

sentences.zh: 今不若畜士眾之力，先為固守。

translations.literal: Now it is better to husband the soldiers' strength and first hold fast in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Better to conserve our troops' strength and dig in for a defensive stand first.

sentences.zh: 彼欲戰不得，攻又不能，其勢必離散。

translations.literal: They will wish to fight but cannot, attack but cannot succeed—their momentum is sure to scatter.
translations.idiomatic: They will want to give battle but be unable to, and want to assault us but fail. Their force will inevitably disperse.

sentences.zh: 然後選精銳，據要害，擊之可破也。

translations.literal: Then choose crack troops, hold the key positions, and strike them—they can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Then pick our best men, seize the vital points, and strike—we can break them.

sentences.zh: 」岱不從，遂與戰，果為所殺。

translations.literal: Dai would not heed this and thereupon gave battle; he was indeed killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai refused to listen and gave battle anyway—and was killed, as predicted.

sentences.zh: 曹操部將東郡陳宮謂操曰：「州今無主，而王命斷絕，宮請說州中綱紀，明府尋往牧之，資之以收天下，此霸王之業也。

translations.literal: Chen Gong of Dong Commandery, an officer under Cao Cao, said to Cao: "The province now has no lord, and royal orders are cut off. Gong asks permission to persuade the leaders of the province; Your Excellency should soon go to govern it, using it as capital to take all under Heaven—this is the enterprise of a hegemon-king."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong of Dong Commandery, an officer in Cao Cao's service, said, "Yan Province is headless and the court's authority no longer reaches us. Let me win over the provincial elite; then you can take up the governorship and use it as a base to bring the realm under your banner—this is how hegemons are made."

sentences.zh: 」宮因往說別駕、治中曰：「今天下分裂而州無主；

translations.literal: Gong thereupon went to persuade the Controller and the Chief Clerk, saying: "Today the realm is split and the province has no lord;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong then went to the Controller and Chief Clerk and said, "The empire is fractured and this province has no ruler;

sentences.zh: 曹東郡，命世之才也，若迎以牧州，必寧生民。

translations.literal: Cao of Dong Commandery is a talent of his generation; if we welcome him to govern the province, the people will surely be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao of Dong Commandery is a man born for his times. If we install him as governor, the people will know peace."

sentences.zh: 」鮑信等亦以為然，乃與州吏萬潛等至東郡，迎操領兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Bao Xin and others also deemed this right and thereupon, with provincial clerks Wan Qian and others, went to Dong Commandery to welcome Cao to head the office of Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xin and the others agreed. Together with provincial officials including Wan Qian, they traveled to Dong Commandery and invited Cao Cao to assume the post of Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 操遂進兵擊黃巾於壽張東。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon advanced troops to strike the Yellow Turbans east of Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao thereupon marched against the Yellow Turbans east of Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 不利。

translations.literal: It went ill for him.
translations.idiomatic: The initial encounter went badly for him.

sentences.zh: 賊眾精悍，操兵寡弱，操撫循激勵，明設賞罰，承間設奇，晝夜會戰，戰輒禽獲，賊遂退走。

translations.literal: The bandits were numerous, spirited, and tough; Cao's troops were few and weak. Cao comforted and encouraged them, clearly set rewards and punishments, seized intervals to lay stratagems, fought day and night in assembly, and whenever they fought captured enemies; the bandits then retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were numerous and fierce, while Cao Cao's force was small and overmatched. He steadied and roused his men, made rewards and punishments explicit, seized every opening for surprise attacks, and fought ceaselessly day and night. In each encounter his troops took prisoners, and the rebels eventually broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 鮑信戰死，操購求其喪不得，乃刻木如信狀，祭而哭焉。

translations.literal: Bao Xin died in battle. Cao offered a reward to recover his body but could not obtain it; he then carved wood in Xin's likeness, sacrificed, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xin fell in battle. Cao Cao offered a rich reward for recovery of his body but could not find it, so he had a wooden effigy carved in Bao Xin's likeness and held funeral rites over it, weeping as he mourned.

sentences.zh: 詔以京兆金尚為兗州刺史，將之部，操逆擊之，尚奔袁術。

translations.literal: An imperial order appointed Jin Shang of Jingzhao Inspector of Yan Province; as he was proceeding to his post, Cao intercepted and attacked him; Shang fled to Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Jin Shang of Jingzhao as Inspector of Yan Province and sent him to take up his post. Cao Cao moved to block him, and Shang fled to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 五月，以征西將軍皇甫嵩為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, General Who Subdues the West Huangfu Song was made Chariots-and-Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the emperor appointed Huangfu Song, General Who Subdues the West, as Chariot-and-Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 初，呂布勸王允盡殺董卓部曲，允曰：「此輩無罪，不可。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lü Bu urged Wang Yun to kill all of Dong Zhuo's followers to the last man. Yun said: "These men are not guilty—it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lü Bu urged Wang Yun to slaughter every last follower of Dong Zhuo. Wang Yun replied, "These men are innocent. That cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 」布欲以卓財物班賜公卿、將校，允又不從。

translations.literal: Bu wished to distribute Zhuo's goods and wealth as gifts to the ministers and commanders; Yun again would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu wanted to distribute Dong Zhuo's treasure among the ministers and officers, but Wang Yun refused that as well.

sentences.zh: 允素以劍客遇布，布負其功勞，多自誇伐，既失意望，漸不相平。

translations.literal: Yun had always treated Bu as a sword-for-hire; Bu relied on his merit, often boasting of himself; having lost what he hoped for, they gradually became estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun had always treated Lü Bu as a hired blade. Lü Bu, proud of his exploits, boasted constantly; when his expectations went unmet, the two men grew increasingly at odds.

sentences.zh: 允性剛稜疾惡，初懼董卓，故折節下之。

translations.literal: Yun's nature was stern and angular, hating evil; at first he feared Dong Zhuo and therefore bent himself to defer below him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun was rigid and unforgiving by nature. At first he had feared Dong Zhuo and so had humbled himself before him.

sentences.zh: 卓既殲滅，自謂無復患難，頗自驕傲，以是群下不甚附之。

translations.literal: Once Zhuo was destroyed, he considered that he had no further troubles and became rather proud and arrogant; because of this his subordinates did not greatly attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dong Zhuo was gone, he believed himself free of all danger and grew arrogant. His subordinates therefore gave him little real loyalty.

sentences.zh: 允始與士孫瑞議，特下詔赦卓部曲，既而疑曰：「部曲從其主耳。

translations.literal: Yun had at first discussed with Shisun Rui and specially issued an edict pardoning Zhuo's followers; then he doubted and said: "Followers obey their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun had first consulted Shisun Rui and issued a special edict pardoning Dong Zhuo's followers. Then he had second thoughts and said, "Retainers follow their master.

sentences.zh: 今若名之惡逆而赦之，恐適使深自疑，非所以安之也。

translations.literal: Now if we label them traitors and yet pardon them, I fear we will only make them deeply suspicious—it is not the way to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: If we brand them traitors and then pardon them, we will only drive them to deep suspicion. That is no way to win their trust."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: He thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 又議悉罷其軍，或說允曰：「涼州人素憚袁氏而畏關東，今若一旦解兵開關，必人人自危。

translations.literal: They also discussed disbanding all their armies entirely. Someone said to Yun: "The men of Liang Province have always feared the Yuan clan and dreaded the east of the passes. If now in a single stroke we disband the troops and open the passes, every man is sure to feel himself in peril."
translations.idiomatic: They also debated disbanding the armies altogether. Someone advised Wang Yun, "The Liangzhou men have long feared the Yuan family and dread the coalition east of the passes. If we disarm them and open the passes in one stroke, every man among them will panic."

sentences.zh: 可以皇甫義真為將軍，就領其眾，因使留陝以安撫之。

translations.literal: We can make Huangfu Yizhen general, have him take command of their masses on the spot, and thereby have him remain at Shan to pacify and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Huangfu Song—Yizhen—as their general, let him take command of them in place, and keep him at Shan to reassure and control them."

sentences.zh: 」允曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun said, "No.

sentences.zh: 關東舉義兵者，皆吾徒也。

translations.literal: Those east of the passes who raised righteous troops are all our own comrades.
translations.idiomatic: The men who raised righteous armies east of the passes are our own allies.

sentences.zh: 今若距險屯陝，雖安涼州，而疑關東之心，不可也。

translations.literal: If now we hold the defiles and encamp at Shan, although we would settle Liang Province, we would arouse suspicion in the hearts of the east of the passes—it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: If we now hold the passes and camp at Shan, we may calm Liangzhou but we will sow doubt among our allies in the east. That will not do."

sentences.zh: 時百姓訛言當悉誅涼州人，卓故將校遂轉相恐動，皆擁兵自守，更相謂曰：「蔡伯喈但以董公親厚，尚從坐，今既不赦我曹而欲使解兵，今日解兵，明日當復為魚肉矣！

translations.literal: At the time the common people spread false rumors that all men of Liang Province were to be put to death. Zhuo's former commanders and officers thereupon grew fearful in turn, all holding troops to guard themselves, and said to one another: "Cai Bojie was punished only because he was close to Lord Dong—yet he was implicated. Now that they neither pardon us but wish us to disband our troops—if we disband today, tomorrow we shall again be fish on the chopping block!"
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread among the people that every man from Liangzhou was to be executed. Dong Zhuo's former officers, growing fearful in turn, all kept their troops under arms. They said to one another, "Even Cai Yong was punished merely for his closeness to Dong Zhuo. Now they refuse to pardon us yet demand we lay down our arms. Disarm today, and tomorrow we are meat on the block!"

sentences.zh: 」呂布使李肅至陝，以詔命誅牛輔，輔等逆與肅戰，肅敗，走弘農，布誅殺之。

translations.literal: Lü Bu sent Li Su to Shan with an edict ordering the execution of Niu Fu. Fu and others turned and fought Su; Su was defeated, fled to Hongnong, and Bu had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu sent Li Su to Shan with an edict commanding the execution of Niu Fu. Niu Fu and his men resisted and fought Li Su, who was defeated and fled to Hongnong, where Lü Bu had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 輔恇怯失守，會營中無故自驚，輔欲走，為左右所殺。

translations.literal: Fu was timid and cowardly and lost his hold. By chance the camp was startled without cause; Fu wished to flee and was killed by those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Fu was timid and lost control of his camp. When the encampment panicked without apparent cause, he tried to flee and was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 李傕等還，輔已死，傕等無所依，遣使詣長安求赦。

translations.literal: Li Jue and others returned; Fu was already dead. Jue and the others had nowhere to rely on and sent envoys to Chang'an to seek a pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his fellows returned to find Niu Fu already dead. With nowhere to turn, they sent envoys to Chang'an to beg for a pardon.

sentences.zh: 王允曰：「一歲不可再赦。

translations.literal: Wang Yun said: "In one year there cannot be a second amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun said, "There cannot be two general amnesties in a single year."

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: He did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 傕等益懼，不知所為，欲各解散，間行歸鄉里，討虜校尉武威賈詡曰：「諸君若棄軍單行，則一亭長能束君矣。

translations.literal: Jue and the others grew more fearful, not knowing what to do, and wished each to disband and return home by secret paths. Jia Xu, Colonel Who Punishes the Barbarians of Wuwei, said: "If you gentlemen abandon your armies and travel alone, then a single village headman can bind you."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his men grew still more afraid and did not know what to do. They thought of disbanding and slipping home by back roads. Jia Xu, Colonel Who Punishes the Barbarians of Wuwei, said, "If you abandon your armies and travel alone, a village headman can arrest you."

sentences.zh: 不如相率而西，以攻長安，為董公報仇。

translations.literal: It would be better to join together and go west to attack Chang'an and avenge Lord Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Better to march west together, attack Chang'an, and avenge Lord Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 事濟，奉國家以正天下；

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds, serve the state to set the realm right;
translations.idiomatic: If we succeed, we can serve the dynasty and set the realm to rights;

sentences.zh: 若其不合，走未後也。

translations.literal: if it does not succeed, flight is not yet too late.
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, we can still flee in time."

sentences.zh: 」傕等然之，乃相與結盟，率軍數千，晨夜西行。

translations.literal: Jue and the others approved this, thereupon swore alliance together, and led several thousand troops west day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and the others agreed. They formed an alliance, mustered several thousand men, and marched west day and night.

sentences.zh: 王允以胡文才、楊整修皆涼州大人，召使東，解釋之，不假以溫顏，謂曰：「關東鼠子，欲何為邪？

translations.literal: Wang Yun, because Hu Wencai and Yang Zhengxiu were both great men of Liang Province, summoned them east to explain matters to them, but did not grant them a warm countenance and said: "The rats east of the passes—what do they intend?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun summoned Hu Wencai and Yang Zhengxiu, both influential men from Liangzhou, to come east and reason with the rebels, but he showed them no kindness and said, "Those rats east of the passes—what do they think they are doing?"

sentences.zh: 卿往呼之！

translations.literal: You go summon them back!
translations.idiomatic: Go call them off!"

sentences.zh: 」於是二人往，實召兵而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two men went—and in fact summoned troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The two men went—and in fact rallied troops and returned with them.

sentences.zh: 傕隨道收兵，比至長安，已十餘萬，與卓故部曲樊稠、李蒙等合圍長安城，城峻不可攻，守之八日。

translations.literal: Jue gathered troops along the road; by the time they reached Chang'an they already numbered more than a hundred thousand. They joined with Zhuo's former followers Fan Chou, Li Meng, and others to besiege Chang'an city. The walls were steep and could not be assaulted; they besieged it for eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue gathered forces along the march, and by the time he reached Chang'an his army exceeded one hundred thousand. He joined Dong Zhuo's former followers Fan Chou and Li Meng in besieging the capital. The walls were too strong to storm, so they settled into an eight-day siege.

sentences.zh: 呂布軍有叟兵內反，六月，戊午，引傕眾入城，放兵虜掠。

translations.literal: In Lü Bu's army some Sou troops rebelled from within. In the sixth month, on the day wuwu, they led Jue's masses into the city and loosed the troops to plunder and carry off captives.
translations.idiomatic: Some Sou auxiliaries in Lü Bu's army mutinied from within. On wuwu day in the sixth month they admitted Li Jue's troops into the city, and the soldiers were turned loose to loot and pillage.

sentences.zh: 布與戰城中，不勝，將數百騎以卓頭繫馬鞍出走，駐馬青瑣門外，招王允同去。

translations.literal: Bu fought them in the city but did not prevail. He led several hundred horsemen, with Zhuo's head tied to his saddle, and fled. He halted his horse outside the Green Lattice Gate and summoned Wang Yun to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fought them inside the city but was defeated. He fled with a few hundred horsemen, Dong Zhuo's severed head tied to his saddle, and halted outside the Green Lattice Gate to urge Wang Yun to flee with him.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「若蒙社稷之靈，上安國家，吾之願也；

translations.literal: Yun said: "If, through the spirits of the altars of soil and grain, above the state is settled, that is my wish;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun said, "If the spirits of the realm grant it and the dynasty is restored, that is my wish;

sentences.zh: 如其不獲，則奉身以死之。

translations.literal: if it is not obtained, then I offer my person and die for it.
translations.idiomatic: if not, I will give my life for it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷幼少，恃我而已，臨難苟免，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: The court is young and small and relies on me alone; to seek escape at the hour of peril—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The court is a child who depends on me alone. I cannot bring myself to flee in the hour of danger.

sentences.zh: 努力謝關東諸公，勤以國家為念！

translations.literal: Strive to convey my thanks to the lords east of the passes and urge them to keep the state ever in mind!
translations.idiomatic: Give my thanks to the lords east of the passes, and urge them to keep the realm foremost in their hearts!"

sentences.zh: 」太常種拂曰：「為國大臣，不能禁暴禦侮，使白刃向宮，去將安之！

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies Zhong Fu said: "As great ministers of the state, unable to restrain violence and repel insult, we have let naked blades turn toward the palace—where shall we go if we leave!"
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies Zhong Fu said, "As ministers of state we failed to check violence and ward off outrage until blades were turned on the palace. Where can we flee?"

sentences.zh: 」遂戰而死。

translations.literal: He thereupon fought and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought and was killed.

sentences.zh: 傕、汜屯南宮掖門，殺太僕魯馗、大鴻臚周奐、城門校尉崔烈、越騎校尉王頎。

translations.literal: Jue and Si encamped at the Southern Palace side gate and killed the Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Kui, the Grand Herald Zhou Huan, the Colonel of the City Gates Cui Lie, and the Colonel of Agile Cavalry Wang Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si camped at the Southern Palace side gate and killed the Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Kui, the Grand Herald Zhou Huan, the Colonel of the City Gates Cui Lie, and the Colonel of Agile Cavalry Wang Qi.

sentences.zh: 吏民死者萬餘人，狼藉滿道。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners who died numbered more than ten thousand; corpses lay strewn full along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand officials and civilians were killed, and the streets were heaped with the dead.

sentences.zh: 王允扶帝上宣平門避兵，傕等於城門下伏地叩頭，帝謂傕等曰：「卿等放兵縱橫，欲何為乎？

translations.literal: Wang Yun supported the emperor up to Xuankang Gate to avoid the troops. Jue and the others prostrated themselves below the gate and knocked their heads. The emperor said to Jue and the others: "You have loosed troops to run riot—what do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun escorted the emperor to Xuankang Gate to escape the fighting. Li Jue and his men kowtowed below the gate. The emperor said to them, "You have turned your soldiers loose to run riot—what do you want?"

sentences.zh: 」傕等曰：「董卓忠於陛下，而無故為呂布所殺，臣等為卓報仇，非敢為逆也。

translations.literal: Jue and the others said: "Dong Zhuo was loyal to Your Majesty yet was killed without cause by Lü Bu. Your servants avenge Zhuo—we do not dare to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Dong Zhuo was loyal to Your Majesty, yet Lü Bu killed him without cause. We seek vengeance for Lord Dong—we do not mean rebellion."

sentences.zh: 請事畢詣廷尉受罪。

translations.literal: We ask, when the affair is finished, to go to the Commandant of Justice to accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When our business is done we will present ourselves to the Commandant of Justice to accept punishment."

sentences.zh: 」傕等圍門樓，共表請司徒王允出，問：「太師何罪？

translations.literal: Jue and the others surrounded the gate tower and jointly memorialized requesting the Minister over the Masses Wang Yun come out, asking: "What was the Grand Mentor's crime?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his men surrounded the gate tower and jointly petitioned for Minister of Education Wang Yun to come out, demanding, "What crime had the Grand Mentor committed?"

sentences.zh: 」允窮蹙，乃下見之。

translations.literal: Yun was cornered and thereupon came down to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, trapped, came down to face them.

sentences.zh: 己未，赦天下，以李傕為揚武將軍，郭汜為揚烈將軍，樊稠等皆為中郎將。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei there was an amnesty for all under Heaven. Li Jue was made General Who Displays Martiality; Guo Si was made General Who Displays Valor; Fan Chou and others were all made Masters of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty. Li Jue was appointed General Who Displays Martiality, Guo Si General Who Displays Valor, and Fan Chou and the rest were made Masters of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 傕等收司隸校尉黃琬，下獄。

translations.literal: Jue and the others seized Colonel Director of Retainers Huang Wan and cast him into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his men arrested Colonel Director of Retainers Huang Wan and threw him into prison.

sentences.zh: 殺之。

translations.literal: They killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They executed him.

sentences.zh: 初，王允以同郡宋翼為左馮翊，王宏為右扶風，傕等欲殺允，恐二郡為患，乃先徵翼、宏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Yun had appointed Song Yi of his native commandery Left Administrator of Fengyi and Wang Hong Right Administrator of Fufeng. Jue and the others wished to kill Yun but feared the two commanderies would become a menace; they therefore first summoned Yi and Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Yun had appointed fellow natives Song Yi as Administrator of Left Fengyi and Wang Hong as Administrator of Right Fufeng. Li Jue and his men wanted to kill Wang Yun but feared trouble from those two commanderies, so they summoned Song Yi and Wang Hong first.

sentences.zh: 宏遣使謂翼曰：「郭汜、李傕以我二人在外，故未危王公。

translations.literal: Hong sent a messenger to say to Yi: "Guo Si and Li Jue, because we two are outside, have not yet endangered Lord Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong sent a messenger to Song Yi: "Guo Si and Li Jue have not yet harmed Lord Wang because we two are still outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 今日就徵，明日俱族，計將安出？

translations.literal: If today we obey the summons, tomorrow we shall both be exterminated as clans—what plan can get us out?"
translations.idiomatic: Obey the summons today, and tomorrow our whole clans are dead. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「雖禍福難量，然王命，所不得避也！

translations.literal: Yi said: "Although fortune and disaster are hard to measure, yet the royal command is what one cannot evade!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Yi replied, "Fortune and disaster may be beyond reckoning, but a royal summons cannot be refused!"

sentences.zh: 」宏曰：「關東義兵鼎沸，欲誅董卓，今卓已死，其黨與易制耳。

translations.literal: Hong said: "The righteous troops east of the passes boil like a cauldron, wishing to execute Dong Zhuo. Now Zhuo is already dead; his partisans are easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong said, "Righteous armies east of the passes are seething to destroy Dong Zhuo. Zhuo is dead, and his remnant bands are easy to subdue.

sentences.zh: 若舉兵共討傕等，與山東相應，此轉禍為福之計也。

translations.literal: If we raise troops jointly to attack Jue and the others and coordinate with the Shandong region, this is the plan to turn misfortune into fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Raise troops together against Li Jue and his fellows and coordinate with the east—that is how we turn disaster into deliverance."

sentences.zh: 」翼不從，宏不能獨立，遂俱就徵。

translations.literal: Yi would not follow; Hong could not act alone and thereupon both obeyed the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yi refused. Wang Hong could not act alone, so both answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 甲子，傕收允及翼、宏，並殺之；

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Jue seized Yun together with Yi and Hong and killed them all;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Li Jue arrested Wang Yun along with Song Yi and Wang Hong and executed them all;

sentences.zh: 允妻子皆死。

translations.literal: Yun's wife and children all died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun's wife and children were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 宏臨命詬曰：「宋翼豎儒，不足議大計！

translations.literal: Hong at the hour of death cursed, saying: "Song Yi is a petty pedant, unfit to discuss great plans!"
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Wang Hong cursed him: "Song Yi, you petty pedant—you were unfit to discuss great affairs!"

sentences.zh: 」傕屍王允於市，莫敢收者，故吏平陵令京兆趙戩棄官收而葬之。

translations.literal: Jue exposed Wang Yun's corpse in the market; no one dared recover it. His former subordinate Zhao Yan of Jingzhao, Magistrate of Pingling, resigned his office, recovered the body, and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue exposed Wang Yun's corpse in the marketplace, and no one dared claim it. Zhao Yan of Jingzhao, a former subordinate and magistrate of Pingling, resigned his post, recovered the body, and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 始，允自專討卓之勞，士孫瑞歸功不侯，故得免於難。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Yun monopolized the merit of punishing Zhuo for himself; Shisun Rui declined credit and was not enfeoffed, and therefore escaped the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: From the first Wang Yun had kept the credit for overthrowing Dong Zhuo to himself. Shisun Rui had declined reward and enfeoffment, and so escaped the slaughter.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：《易》稱「勞謙君子有終吉」，士孫瑞有功不伐，以保其身，可不謂之智乎！

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: The Changes states, "The laboring, modest noble has a conclusion of good fortune." Shisun Rui had merit yet did not boast, and thereby preserved his person—can this fail to be called wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: The Book of Changes says, "The laboring, modest noble attains good fortune in the end." Shisun Rui had merit yet did not boast of it, and so preserved his life—was that not wisdom?

sentences.zh: 傕等以賈詡為左馮翊，欲侯之。

translations.literal: Jue and the others made Jia Xu Administrator of Left Fengyi and wished to enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his men appointed Jia Xu Administrator of Left Fengyi and wished to ennoble him.

sentences.zh: 詡曰：「此救命之計，何功之有！

translations.literal: Xu said: "This was a plan to save our lives—what merit is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu said, "That was a plan to save our lives—what merit is there in it?"

sentences.zh: 」固辭不受。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 又以為尚書僕射，詡曰：「尚書僕射，官之師長，天下所望，詡名不素重，非所以服人也。

translations.literal: They also wished to make him Vice Director of the Masters of Writing. Xu said: "The Vice Director of the Masters of Writing is the chief officer among officials, what all under Heaven looks to. Xu's name is not by nature weighty—it is not the means to make people submit."
translations.idiomatic: They next offered him the post of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing. Jia Xu said, "That office is the chief among officials and the object of the realm's expectations. My name carries no established weight—I am not fit to command men's respect."

sentences.zh: 」乃以為尚書。

translations.literal: They thereupon made him Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Master of Writing instead.

sentences.zh: 呂布自武關奔南陽，袁術待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Lü Bu fled from Wu Pass to Nanyang; Yuan Shu treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fled through Wu Pass to Nanyang, where Yuan Shu received him with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 布自恃有功於袁氏，恣兵鈔掠。

translations.literal: Bu relied on his merit toward the Yuan clan and let his troops plunder at will.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu, counting on his service to the Yuan family, let his soldiers loot at will.

sentences.zh: 術患之，布不自安，去從張楊於河內。

translations.literal: Shu was troubled by this; Bu did not feel secure and left to join Zhang Yang in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu grew alarmed. Uneasy, Lü Bu left and joined Zhang Yang in Henei.

sentences.zh: 李傕等購求布急，布又逃歸袁紹。

translations.literal: Li Jue and the others urgently offered a reward to seek Bu; Bu again fled and returned to Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his men offered a rich bounty for his capture. Lü Bu fled again and took refuge with Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以前將軍趙謙為司徒。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the former General of the Front Zhao Qian was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day the former General of the Front Zhao Qian was appointed Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子，以太尉馬日磾為太傅，錄尚書事；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day gengzi, the Grand Commandant Ma Midi was made Grand Tutor and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on gengzi day, Grand Commandant Ma Midi was appointed Grand Tutor with authority to oversee the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 八月，以車騎將軍皇甫嵩為太尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Chariots-and-Cavalry General Huangfu Song was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Chariot-and-Cavalry General Huangfu Song was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 詔太傅馬日磾、太僕趙岐杖節鎮撫關東。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Tutor Ma Midi and Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhao Qi to bear staffs of authority and pacify the east of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Grand Tutor Ma Midi and Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhao Qi to proceed east of the passes with imperial staffs of authority to restore order.

sentences.zh: 九月，以李傕為車騎將軍、領司隸校尉、假節；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Li Jue was made Chariots-and-Cavalry General, acting Colonel Director of Retainers, with credential staff;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Li Jue was appointed Chariot-and-Cavalry General, acting Colonel Director of Retainers, with credential staff;

sentences.zh: 郭汜為後將軍，樊稠為右將軍，張濟為驃騎將軍，皆封侯。

translations.literal: Guo Si was made General of the Rear; Fan Chou was made General of the Right; Zhang Ji was made General of Fast Cavalry—all were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si was made General of the Rear, Fan Chou General of the Right, and Zhang Ji General of Fast Cavalry; all were ennobled as marquises.

sentences.zh: 傕、汜、稠筦朝政，濟出屯弘農。

translations.literal: Jue, Si, and Chou managed court government; Ji went out to encamp at Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue, Guo Si, and Fan Chou controlled the government; Zhang Ji camped at Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 司徒趙謙罷。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Zhao Qian was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Zhao Qian was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以司空淳於嘉為司徒，光祿大夫楊彪為司空，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Minister of Works Chunyu Jia was made Minister over the Masses; Household Counsellor Yang Biao was made Minister of Works and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day, Minister of Works Chunyu Jia was appointed Minister of Education, and Household Counsellor Yang Biao was made Minister of Works with authority to oversee the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初，董卓入關，說韓遂、馬騰與共圖山東，遂、騰率眾詣長安，會卓死，李傕等以遂為鎮西將軍，遣還金城；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Dong Zhuo entered the passes, he persuaded Han Sui and Ma Teng to join him in plotting the Shandong region. Sui and Teng led their masses to Chang'an. When Zhuo died, Li Jue and the others made Sui General Who Guards the West and sent him back to Jincheng;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Dong Zhuo entered the passes, he had persuaded Han Sui and Ma Teng to join him against the east. They marched to Chang'an with their forces. After Zhuo's death, Li Jue and his men appointed Han Sui General Who Guards the West and sent him back to Jincheng;

sentences.zh: 騰為征西將軍，遣屯郿。

translations.literal: Teng was made General Who Campaigns West and was sent to encamp at Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng was made General Who Campaigns West and stationed at Mei.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，荊州刺史劉表遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Inspector of Jing Province Liu Biao sent envoys with tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Liu Biao, Inspector of Jing Province, sent envoys bearing tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 以表為鎮南將軍、荊州牧，封成武侯。

translations.literal: Biao was made General Who Guards the South and Governor of Jing Province and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Guards the South and Governor of Jing Province and ennobled as Marquis of Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太尉皇甫嵩免，以光祿大夫周忠為太尉，參錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Grand Commandant Huangfu Song was dismissed; Household Counsellor Zhou Zhong was made Grand Commandant and participated in recording affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Grand Commandant Huangfu Song was dismissed. Household Counsellor Zhou Zhong was appointed Grand Commandant with authority to assist in overseeing the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 曹操追黃巾至濟北，悉降之，得戎卒三十餘萬，男女百餘萬口，收其精銳者，號青州兵。

translations.literal: Cao Cao pursued the Yellow Turbans to Jibei and received the surrender of them all. He obtained more than three hundred thousand fighting troops and over a million men and women. He selected their crack troops and styled them the Qing Province Army.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pursued the Yellow Turbans into Jibei and accepted the surrender of the whole force—more than three hundred thousand fighting men and over a million civilians. He took their best troops into service and called them the Qingzhou Army.

sentences.zh: 操辟陳留毛玠為治中從事，玠言於操曰：「今天下分崩，乘輿播蕩，生民廢業，饑饉流亡，公家無經歲之儲，百姓無安固之志，難以持久。

translations.literal: Cao recruited Mao Jie of Chenliu as Controller Staff Officer. Jie said to Cao: "Today the realm is split apart; the imperial carriage is tossed about; the living people have abandoned their occupations; famine and flight prevail; the public treasury has no stores to last a year; the common people have no will to settle securely—it is hard to endure long."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao recruited Mao Jie of Chenliu as Controller Staff Officer. Mao Jie told him, "The realm is shattered, the emperor driven from his seat, the people idle in their fields, famine and exile everywhere. The treasury has no stores to last a year, and the common folk have no heart to settle. Such a state cannot endure."

sentences.zh: 夫兵義者勝，守位以財，宜奉天子以令不臣，修耕植以畜軍資，如此，則霸王之業可成也。

translations.literal: Now, troops with righteousness prevail; one holds position by wealth. It is fitting to serve the Son of Heaven to command those who are not ministers, and to cultivate farming and planting to store military supplies—thus the enterprise of a hegemon-king can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Armies that fight in a just cause prevail, and power rests on wealth. You should hold the emperor aloft to command the disloyal, promote farming to build up military stores—and then the work of a true hegemon can be achieved."

sentences.zh: 」操納其言，遣使詣河內太守張楊，欲假塗西至長安，楊不聽。

translations.literal: " Cao accepted his words, dispatched envoys to go to Henei Administrator Zhang Yang, wishing to borrow the road west to Chang'an; Yang would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took his counsel and sent envoys to Zhang Yang, Administrator of Henei, asking passage west to Chang'an. Zhang Yang refused.

sentences.zh: 定陶董昭說楊曰：「袁、曹雖為一家，勢不久群。

translations.literal: Dingtao Dong Zhao said to Yang: "Yuan and Cao, though of one household, their power cannot long remain united.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao of Dingtao said to Zhang Yang, "Yuan Shao and Cao Cao may be kin by marriage, but their alliance cannot last.

sentences.zh: 曹今雖弱，然實天下之英雄也，當故結之。

translations.literal: Cao is weak now, but in truth he is a hero of all under Heaven; one ought to befriend him for old times' sake.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao is weak now, yet he is truly a hero of the age. You should win him as an ally while you still can.

sentences.zh: 況今有緣，宜通其上事，並表薦之，若事有成，永為深分。

translations.literal: Moreover, there is opportunity now—it is fitting to relay his business above and jointly memorialize recommending him; if things succeed, there will be a deep bond forever.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, fate has brought him to your door. Relay his petition to the court and recommend him in your own memorial. If all goes well, you will share a bond that lasts.

sentences.zh: 」楊是通操上事，仍表薦操。

translations.literal: " Yang thereupon relayed Cao's business upward and also memorialized recommending Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang did so: he forwarded Cao Cao's petition to the court and memorialized in his favor.

sentences.zh: 昭為操作書與李傕、郭汜等，各隨輕重致殷勤。

translations.literal: Zhao wrote letters for Cao to Li Jue, Guo Si, and others, each according to rank showing earnest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao drafted letters from Cao Cao to Li Jue, Guo Si, and the rest, tailoring each message to its recipient's stature and station.

sentences.zh: 傕、汜見操使，以為關東欲自立天子，今曹操雖有使命，非其誠實，議留操使。

translations.literal: Li Jue and Guo Si, seeing Cao's envoy, thought the east of the Pass wished to set up its own Son of Heaven; though Cao Cao now had a mission, it was not sincere—they debated detaining Cao's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jue and Guo Si received Cao Cao's envoy, they suspected the eastern lords of plotting to enthrone their own emperor. Though Cao bore an imperial commission, they judged it a sham and debated holding his envoy hostage.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎鐘繇說傕、汜曰：「方今英雄並起，各矯命專制，唯曹兗州乃心王室，而逆其忠款，非所以副將來之望也？

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Zhong Yao said to Li Jue and Guo Si: "Now heroes rise together, each forging orders and ruling alone—only Cao of Yan Province is loyal to the royal house; to go against his loyal sincerity—is this not to fall short of what the future hopes for?"
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Zhong Yao urged them, "Heroes rise on every side, each forging edicts and ruling as he pleases. Only the Governor of Yan Province, Cao Cao, still serves the throne in good faith. To spurn his loyalty—will that not disappoint every man who still hopes for the dynasty's restoration?"

sentences.zh: 」傕、汜乃厚加報答。

translations.literal: " Li Jue and Guo Si then responded generously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si then sent Cao Cao a generous reply.

sentences.zh: 繇，皓之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yao was Hao's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao was the great-grandson of Zhong Hao.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史陶謙與諸守相共奏記，推朱儁為太師，因移檄牧伯，欲以同討李傕等，奉迎天子。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Inspector Tao Qian together with various administrators and chiefs jointly submitted a memorial, proposing Zhu Jun as Grand Preceptor, and issued a proclamation to the provincial governors, wishing to join in attacking Li Jue and others and escort the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou Inspector Tao Qian joined the local administrators in a joint memorial proposing Zhu Jun as Grand Preceptor. They also sent proclamations to the provincial governors, calling for a united campaign against Li Jue and his faction and for escorting the emperor home.

sentences.zh: 會李傕用太尉周忠、尚書賈詡策，徵儁入朝，儁乃辭謙議而就徵，復為太僕。

translations.literal: Just then Li Jue used Grand Commandant Zhou Zhong's and Minister Jia Xu's stratagem, summoning Zhu Jun to court; Zhu Jun then declined Tao Qian's plan and answered the summons, again becoming Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue, acting on a plan from Grand Commandant Zhou Zhong and Minister Jia Xu, summoned Zhu Jun to court. Zhu Jun set aside Tao Qian's scheme, accepted the summons, and was reappointed Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚復遣兵擊袁紹，至龍水奏，紹擊破之。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan again sent troops to attack Yuan Shao, reaching Long River Zou; Shao defeated and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan again sent troops against Yuan Shao and advanced as far as Long River Zou. Yuan Shao routed him.

sentences.zh: 瓚遂幽州，不敢復出。

translations.literal: Zan retreated to You Province and dared not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Zan withdrew into You Province and did not dare march out again.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史汝南陳溫卒，袁紹使袁遺領揚州；

translations.literal: Yangzhou Inspector Chen Wen of Runan died; Yuan Shao had Yuan Yi take charge of Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen of Runan, Inspector of Yangzhou, died. Yuan Shao appointed his kinsman Yuan Yi to take over the province;

sentences.zh: 袁術擊破之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: but Yuan Shu defeated Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 遺走至沛，為兵所殺。

translations.literal: Yi fled to Pei and was killed by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi fled to Pei, where soldiers killed him.

sentences.zh: 術以下邳陳瑀為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Shu appointed Chen Yu of Xiapi as Yangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu then installed Chen Yu of Xiapi as Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day jia-yin the first of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (jia-yin), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: On ding-mao, amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ding-mao, an amnesty was declared for the empire.

sentences.zh: 曹操軍鄄城。

translations.literal: Cao Cao's army was at Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao encamped at Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 袁術為劉表所逼，引軍屯封丘，黑山別部及匈奴於扶羅皆附之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu, pressed by Liu Biao, led his army to camp at Fengqiu; Black Mountain splinter bands and the Xiongnu Chanyu Yufuluo all attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by Liu Biao, Yuan Shu withdrew to Fengqiu. Splinter bands from the Black Mountain rebels and the Xiongnu chieftain Yufuluo joined him there.

sentences.zh: 曹操擊破術軍，遂圍封丘。

translations.literal: Cao Cao defeated Shu's army and then besieged Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao routed his army and laid siege to Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 術走襄邑，又走寧陵。

translations.literal: Shu fled to Xiangyi, then again to Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu fled to Xiangyi, then to Ningling.

sentences.zh: 操追擊。

translations.literal: Cao pursued and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pursued.

sentences.zh: 連破之。

translations.literal: He defeated them repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Yuan Shu again and again.

sentences.zh: 術走九江，揚州剌史陳瑀拒術不納。

translations.literal: Shu fled to Jiujiang; Yangzhou Inspector Chen Yu refused to admit Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu fled toward Jiujiang, but Chen Yu, Inspector of Yangzhou, refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 術退保陰陵，集兵於淮北，復進向壽春。

translations.literal: Shu withdrew to guard Yinling, gathered troops north of the Huai, and again advanced toward Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to Yinling, rallied troops north of the Huai, and marched again on Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 瑀懼，走歸下邳，術遂領其州，兼稱徐州伯。

translations.literal: Yu feared, fled back to Xiapi; Shu then took over his province and also styled himself Earl of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu fled in fear to Xiapi. Yuan Shu seized control of Yangzhou and styled himself Earl of Xuzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 李傕欲結術為援，以術為左將軍，封陽翟侯，假節。

translations.literal: Li Jue wished to ally with Shu as support, appointed Shu Left General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangzhai, granted the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue sought an alliance with Yuan Shu, appointing him Left General, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Yangzhai, and granting him the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 袁紹與公孫瓚所置青州刺史田楷連戰二年，士卒疲睏，糧食並盡，互掠百姓，野無青草。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan's installed Qingzhou Inspector Tian Kai fought continuously for two years; soldiers weary and worn, grain entirely exhausted, each side plundering the common people—the wilds had no green grass.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Tian Kai, whom Gongsun Zan had installed as Inspector of Qingzhou, fought for two years without respite. Their troops were exhausted, their grain gone. Both armies preyed on the peasants until not a blade of green remained in the fields.

sentences.zh: 紹以其子譚為青州刺史，楷與戰，不勝。

translations.literal: Shao appointed his son Tan as Qingzhou Inspector; Kai fought him and did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao appointed his son Tan Inspector of Qingzhou. Tian Kai gave battle and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 會趙岐來和解關東，瓚乃與紹和親，各引兵去。

translations.literal: When Zhao Qi came to reconcile the east of the Pass, Zan then made peace with Shao by marriage; each withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Qi arrived to mediate among the eastern lords, Gongsun Zan made peace with Yuan Shao through a marriage alliance, and both sides withdrew their armies.

sentences.zh: 三月，袁紹在薄落津。

translations.literal: Third month, Yuan Shao was at Boluo Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yuan Shao was encamped at Boluo Ford.

sentences.zh: 魏郡兵反，與黑山賊於毒等數萬人共覆鄴城，殺其太守。

translations.literal: Wei commandery soldiers rebelled; together with Black Mountain bandit Yu Du and others, tens of thousands, they overran Ye city and killed its administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers of Wei Commandery rose in revolt. Joining Yu Du of the Black Mountain bandits, they mustered tens of thousands of men, stormed Ye, and killed its administrator.

sentences.zh: 紹還屯斥丘。

translations.literal: Shao returned and encamped at Chijiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao withdrew and encamped at Chijiu.

sentences.zh: 夏，曹操還軍定陶。

translations.literal: Summer, Cao Cao returned his army to Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: In summer Cao Cao marched his army back to Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 徐州治中東海王朗及別駕琅邪趙昱說刺史陶謙曰：「求諸侯莫如勤王，今天子越在西京，宜遣使奉貢。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Controller Staff Wang Lang of Donghai and Administrator Staff Zhao Yu of Langye said to Inspector Tao Qian: "To seek enfeoffment as feudal lord, nothing surpasses serving the king—the Son of Heaven is now in the western capital; you should dispatch envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang of Donghai, Controller Staff Officer of Xuzhou, and Zhao Yu of Langye, Administrator Staff Officer, urged Inspector Tao Qian, "If you seek a noble rank, nothing wins it faster than serving the throne. The emperor languishes in the western capital. Send envoys with tribute at once.

sentences.zh: 」謙乃遣昱奉章至長安。

translations.literal: " Qian then sent Yu with memorial to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian sent Zhao Yu to Chang'an with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔拜謙徐州牧，加安東將軍，封溧陽侯。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Qian as Governor of Xuzhou, added General Who Pacifies the East, enfeoffed as Marquis of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict appointed Tao Qian Governor of Xuzhou, promoted him to General Who Pacifies the East, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 以昱為廣陵太守，朗為會稽太守。

translations.literal: Yu was made Administrator of Guangling, Lang of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu was made Administrator of Guangling and Wang Lang of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 是時，徐方百姓殷盛，谷實差豐，流民多歸之。

translations.literal: At this time the people of the Xu region were prosperous, grain fairly abundant, and displaced persons mostly came to them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xu region was populous and its harvests fairly plentiful. Refugees streamed in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 而謙信用讒邪，疏遠忠直，刑政不治，由是徐州漸亂。

translations.literal: But Qian trusted slanderers and the corrupt, kept the loyal and upright at a distance, and penal administration was not well governed—thus Xuzhou gradually fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tao Qian trusted slanderers and the corrupt, kept loyal men at arm's length, and let law and order decay. Xuzhou slowly slid into chaos.

sentences.zh: 許劭避地廣陵，謙禮之甚厚，劭告其徒曰：「陶恭祖外慕聲名，內非真正，待吾雖厚，其勢必薄。

translations.literal: Xu Shao took refuge in Guangling; Qian treated him very generously. Shao told his followers: "Tao Gongzu outwardly covets reputation, inwardly is not truly sincere; though he treats me generously, in time he will surely treat me coldly.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao had taken refuge in Guangling, and Tao Qian honored him lavishly. Shao warned his followers, "Tao Gongzu courts reputation but lacks genuine virtue. He treats me well now, but he will turn on me before long.

sentences.zh: 」遂去之。

translations.literal: " He then left.
translations.idiomatic: He left at once.

sentences.zh: 後謙果捕諸寓士，人乃服其先識。

translations.literal: Later Qian indeed arrested various resident scholars—people then admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tao Qian did arrest the scholars lodging in his domain, and men marveled at Xu Shao's foresight.

sentences.zh: 六月，扶風大雨雹。

translations.literal: Sixth month, in Fufeng great rain and hail.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Fufeng was struck by heavy rain and hail.

sentences.zh: 華山崩裂。

translations.literal: Mount Hua split and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Hua split apart.

sentences.zh: 太尉周忠免，以太僕朱儁為太尉，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhou Zhong was dismissed; Former Chamberlain Zhu Jun was made Grand Commandant, with control of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Zhou Zhong was dismissed. Zhu Jun, lately Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, was appointed Grand Commandant with authority over the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 下邳闕宣聚眾數千人，自稱天子；

translations.literal: At Xiapi, Que Xuan gathered several thousand men and styled himself Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: At Xiapi, Que Xuan gathered several thousand followers and declared himself emperor;

sentences.zh: 陶謙擊殺之。

translations.literal: Tao Qian attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 大雨，晝夜二十餘日，漂沒民居。

translations.literal: Great rain, day and night for more than twenty days, flooding and destroying people's dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell day and night for more than twenty days, flooding homes and drowning whole neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 袁紹出軍入朝歌鹿腸山，討於毒，圍攻五日，破之，斬毒及其眾萬餘級。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao went out with his army into Chaoge's Deer Intestine Mountain, campaigning against Yu Du; besieged five days, broke him, beheaded Du and more than ten thousand of his host.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao marched into the Deer Intestine Hills of Chaoge to campaign against Yu Du. After five days of siege he broke the rebel line, beheaded Yu Du, and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 紹遂尋山北行，進擊諸賊左髭丈八等，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Shao then followed the mountain north, advanced to attack various bandits Left Whiskers Zhangba and others—all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed north along the ridges, hunting bandit chiefs such as Left Whiskers Zhangba, and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 又擊劉石、青牛角、黃龍左校、郭大賢、李大目、於氐根等，復斬數萬級，皆屠其屯壁。

translations.literal: He again attacked Liu Shi, Green Ox Horn, Yellow Dragon Left Commander, Guo Daxian, Li Damu, Yu Digen, and others, again beheading tens of thousands, all slaughtering their fortified camps.
translations.idiomatic: He next struck Liu Shi, Green Ox Horn, Yellow Dragon Left Commander, Guo Daxian, Li Damu, Yu Digen, and others, taking tens of thousands more heads and slaughtering every fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 遂與黑山賊張燕及四營屠各、雁門烏桓戰於常山。

translations.literal: He then fought Black Mountain bandit Zhang Yan and the Four Camps Tuge, Yanmen Wuhuan at Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then met Zhang Yan of the Black Mountain rebels, the Four Camps Tuge, and the Yanmen Wuhuan in battle at Changshan.

sentences.zh: 燕精兵數萬，騎數千匹。

translations.literal: Yan had elite troops numbering tens of thousands, cavalry several thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan fielded tens of thousands of elite infantry and several thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 紹與呂布共擊燕，連戰十餘日，燕兵死傷雖多，紹軍亦疲，遂俱退。

translations.literal: Shao together with Lü Bu attacked Yan; fought more than ten days; though Yan's troops dead and wounded were many, Shao's army also weary—they both withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Lü Bu attacked him together. For more than ten days the battle raged. Zhang Yan's losses were heavy, but Yuan Shao's army was exhausted as well, and both sides withdrew.

sentences.zh: 呂布將士多暴橫，紹患之，布因求還雒陽。

translations.literal: Lü Bu's generals and soldiers were mostly violent and overbearing; Shao was troubled; Bu therefore asked to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's men were violent and unruly, and Yuan Shao grew uneasy. Lü Bu asked leave to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 紹承製以布領司隸校尉，遣壯士送布，而陰圖之。

translations.literal: Shao, acting on imperial authority, had Bu lead the Colonel of the Censorate, sent strong men to escort Bu, while secretly plotting against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao, acting on imperial commission, appointed him Colonel of the Censorate and sent braves to escort him—while secretly plotting his death.

sentences.zh: 布使人鼓箏於帳中，密亡去，送者夜起，斫帳被皆壞。

translations.literal: Bu had someone play the zither in his tent, secretly fled; the escorts rose at night and hacked—the bedding in the tent was all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu left a man playing the zither in his tent and slipped away by night. His escorts woke and hacked at the bedding until the tent was in shreds—only then did they realize he was gone.

sentences.zh: 明旦，紹聞布尚在，懼，閉城自守。

translations.literal: Next dawn Shao heard Bu still lived, feared, closed the city and held himself within.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yuan Shao learned Lü Bu still lived. Terrified, he shut the gates and barred himself inside.

sentences.zh: 布引軍復歸張楊。

translations.literal: Bu led his army back to Zhang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu marched his army back to Zhang Yang.

sentences.zh: 前太尉曹嵩避難在琅邪，其子操令泰山太守應邵迎之。

translations.literal: Former Grand Commandant Cao Song took refuge in Langye; his son Cao ordered Taishan Administrator Ying Shao to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Song, former Grand Commandant, had taken refuge in Langye. His son Cao Cao ordered Ying Shao, Administrator of Taishan, to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 嵩輜重百餘兩，陶謙別將守陰平，士卒利嵩財寶，掩襲嵩於華、費間，殺之，並少子德。

translations.literal: Song had more than a hundred cartloads of baggage; Tao Qian's detached commander guarding Yinping—soldiers coveted Song's treasure, ambushed Song between Hua and Fei, killed him together with his younger son De.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Song traveled with more than a hundred wagons of goods. A detached force of Tao Qian's, stationed at Yinping, coveted the treasure. The soldiers ambushed him between Hua and Fei, killed him, and killed his younger son De as well.

sentences.zh: 秋，操引兵擊謙，攻拔十餘城，至彭城，大戰，謙兵敗，走保郯。

translations.literal: Autumn, Cao led troops against Qian, captured more than ten cities, reached Pengcheng, great battle—Qian's troops defeated, fled to hold Tancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Cao Cao marched against Tao Qian, stormed more than ten cities, and fought a great battle at Pengcheng. Tao Qian was routed and fled to shelter behind the walls of Tan.

sentences.zh: 初，京、雒遭董卓之亂，民流移東出，多依徐土，遇操至，坑殺男女數十萬口於泗水，水為不流。

translations.literal: Initially, the Jing-Luo region suffered Dong Zhuo's chaos; people drifted east, many relying on Xu lands; when Cao arrived, he buried alive men and women numbering hundreds of thousands at the Si River—the water ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong Zhuo's ravages of the capital, countless families had fled east into Xu territory. When Cao Cao arrived, he massacred men and women by the hundreds of thousands along the Si River until the current choked with corpses.

sentences.zh: 操攻郯不能克，乃去，攻取應、睢陵、夏丘，皆屠之，雞犬亦盡，墟邑無復行人。

translations.literal: Cao attacked Tan but could not take it; he then left, attacked and took Ying, Suiling, Xiaqiu—all slaughtered, chickens and dogs too exhausted; ruins and villages had no travelers again.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to take Tan, he turned aside, seized Ying, Suiling, and Xiaqiu, and put each to the sword until not a chicken or dog remained. The roads lay empty and the towns were ruins.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛丑，京師地震。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on xin-chou, the capital earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the day xin-chou of the tenth month, the capital was shaken by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 有星孛於天市。

translations.literal: A broom star appeared in the Celestial Market constellation.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared in the Celestial Market constellation.

sentences.zh: 司空楊彪免。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yang Biao was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao was dismissed from office as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以太常趙溫為司空，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On bing-wu, Grand Minister of Sacrifices Zhao Wen was made Minister of Works, with control of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bing-wu, Zhao Wen, Grand Minister of Sacrifices, was appointed Minister of Works with authority over the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉虞與公孫瓚積不相能，瓚數與袁紹相攻，虞禁之，不可，而稍節其稟假。

translations.literal: Liu Yu and Gongsun Zan long incompatible; Zan repeatedly fought Yuan Shao; Yu forbade it but could not, and gradually reduced his grain allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu and Gongsun Zan had long been at odds. Zan repeatedly clashed with Yuan Shao. Liu Yu forbade it but could not stop him, and slowly cut his grain rations.

sentences.zh: 瓚怒，屢違節度，又復侵犯百姓。

translations.literal: Zan was angry, repeatedly disobeyed regulations, and again encroached on the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Zan grew furious, defied Liu Yu's orders again and again, and preyed on the common people.

sentences.zh: 虞不能制，乃遣驛使奉章陳其暴掠之罪，瓚亦上虞稟糧不周。

translations.literal: Yu could not control him, then sent courier with memorial stating his plundering crimes; Zan also memorialized that Yu's grain provisions were inadequate.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to restrain him, Liu Yu sent a courier with a memorial detailing Zan's pillage. Zan memorialized in turn that Liu Yu had failed to supply his troops.

sentences.zh: 二奏交馳，互相非毀，朝廷依違而已。

translations.literal: The two memorials flew back and forth, each slandering the other—the court merely wavered and did nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials flew back and forth, each man slandering the other. The court wavered and did nothing.

sentences.zh: 瓚乃築小城於薊城東南以居之。

translations.literal: Zan then built a small city southeast of Ji to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Zan built a small fortress southeast of Ji and moved there.

sentences.zh: 虞數請會，瓚輒稱病不應；

translations.literal: Yu repeatedly invited him to meet; Zan always claimed illness and did not respond;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu invited him to parley again and again, but Zan always pleaded illness and refused;

sentences.zh: 虞恐其終為亂，乃率所部兵合十萬人以討之。

translations.literal: Yu feared he would ultimately cause rebellion, then led his division troops totaling a hundred thousand to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zan would bring ruin on the north, Liu Yu mustered a hundred thousand men and marched against him.

sentences.zh: 時瓚部曲放散在外，倉卒掘東城欲走，虞兵無部伍，不習戰，又愛民廬舍，敕不聽焚燒，戒軍士曰：「無傷餘人，殺一伯珪而已。

translations.literal: At that time Zan's retainers were scattered outside; in haste he dug through the eastern wall intending to flee. Yu's troops had no formations, were unskilled in war; he also cherished the people's dwellings—ordered no burning allowed, warned the soldiers: "Do not harm the rest—kill only Bo Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's troops were scattered abroad. He tried to break out through the eastern wall in haste. Liu Yu's men were undisciplined and unused to war. He forbade burning houses and told his soldiers, "Spare the people. Kill only Bo Gui."

sentences.zh: 」攻圍不下。

translations.literal: " The attack and siege did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The siege failed.

sentences.zh: 瓚乃簡募銳士數百人，因風縱火，直衝突之，虞眾大潰。
