translations.literal: Zan then selected several hundred elite troops, took advantage of the wind to set fire, charged straight into them—Yu's host utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Zan chose several hundred elite fighters, set fires downwind, and charged. Liu Yu's army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 虞與官屬北奔居庸，瓚追攻之，三日，城陷，執虞並妻子還薊，猶使領州文書。

translations.literal: Yu with his officials fled north to Juyong; Zan pursued and attacked; three days, the city fell; seized Yu together with wife and children, returned to Ji—still had him handle provincial documents.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu fled north to Juyong with his staff. Zan pursued, and in three days the town fell. He seized Liu Yu, his wife, and his children and brought them back to Ji, yet still had Liu Yu manage the province's paperwork.

sentences.zh: 會詔遣使者段訓增虞封邑，督六州事；

translations.literal: Meanwhile an edict sent envoy Duan Xun to enlarge Yu's fief, supervise six provinces' affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Just then an imperial edict arrived with the envoy Duan Xun, enlarging Liu Yu's fief and placing six provinces under his supervision;

sentences.zh: 拜瓚前將軍，封易侯。

translations.literal: appointed Zan Former General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: and appointing Gongsun Zan Former General and Marquis of Yi.

sentences.zh: 瓚乃誣虞前與袁紹等謀稱尊號，脅訓斬虞及妻子於薊市。

translations.literal: Zan then falsely accused Yu of earlier plotting with Yuan Shao and others to claim exalted titles, coerced Xun to behead Yu and wife and children in Ji market.
translations.idiomatic: Zan then accused Liu Yu of plotting with Yuan Shao to proclaim himself emperor, forced Duan Xun to behead Liu Yu and his family in the market at Ji.

sentences.zh: 故常山相孫瑾、掾張逸、張瓚等相與就虞，罵瓚極口，然後同死，瓚傳虞首於京師，故吏尾敦於路劫虞首，歸葬之。

translations.literal: Former Changshan Chancellor Sun Jin, staff Zhang Yi, Zhang Zan, and others together went to Yu, cursed Zan to the fullest, then died together. Zan sent Yu's head to the capital; former subordinate Wei Dun on the road seized Yu's head and returned to bury it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jin, former Chancellor of Changshan, and the staff officers Zhang Yi and Zhang Zan went to Liu Yu's side, cursed Gongsun Zan to his face, and died with him. Zan sent Liu Yu's head to the capital, but Wei Dun, a former subordinate, waylaid the convoy, recovered the head, and gave it burial.

sentences.zh: 虞以恩厚得眾心，北州百姓流舊莫不痛惜。

translations.literal: Yu by generous kindness won the hearts of the masses; old settlers and common folk of the northern provinces all grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had won the north through kindness. Old settlers and common folk alike mourned him.

sentences.zh: 初，虞欲遣使奉章詣長安，而難其人，眾鹹曰：「右北平田疇，年二十二，年雖少，然有奇材。

translations.literal: Initially Yu wished to dispatch an envoy with memorial to Chang'an but found it hard to choose a man; all said: "Right Beiping Tian Chou, age twenty-two—though young, he has extraordinary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Yu had wished to send a memorial to Chang'an but could find no man fit for the journey. All agreed: "Tian Chou of Right Beiping is only twenty-two, yet he has rare ability."

sentences.zh: 」虞乃備禮，請以為掾。

translations.literal: " Yu then prepared ceremony and invited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu received him with full ceremony and appointed him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 具車騎將行，疇曰：「今道路阻絕，寇虜縱橫，稱官奉使，為眾所指。

translations.literal: Equipped with chariots and cavalry about to depart, Chou said: "Now roads are blocked, bandits and raiders roam—if one claims office as envoy, one becomes the target of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When horses and chariots were ready, Tian Chou said, "The roads are cut, bandits roam everywhere. Travel as an official envoy and every hand will be against you.

sentences.zh: 願以私行，期於得達而已。

translations.literal: I wish to travel privately, aiming only to reach there."
translations.idiomatic: Let me go as a private man. I ask only to arrive."

sentences.zh: 」虞從之。

translations.literal: " Yu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 疇乃自選家客二十騎，俱上西關，出塞，傍北山，直趣朔方，循間道至長安致命。

translations.literal: Chou then himself chose twenty household retainers as cavalry, together ascended the western pass, left the frontier, along the northern mountains straight to Shuofang, followed hidden paths to Chang'an to deliver the message.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou chose twenty household retainers as escort, crossed the western pass, left the frontier, skirted the northern mountains, struck for Shuofang, and by hidden paths reached Chang'an with the memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔拜疇為騎都尉。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chou as Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 疇以天子方蒙塵未安，不可以荷佩榮寵，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Chou considered the Son of Heaven still dust-stained and unsettled—one could not bear honors; firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou held that the emperor, still wandering in exile, was in no state to bestow honors. He firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 得報，馳還，比至，虞已死，疇謁祭虞墓，陳發章表，哭泣而去。

translations.literal: Having received reply, galloped back; by the time he arrived, Yu was already dead. Chou paid respects at Yu's tomb, presented and opened the memorial, wept and departed.
translations.idiomatic: With the court's reply in hand, he raced home. By the time he arrived, Liu Yu was dead. Tian Chou paid his respects at the tomb, presented the memorial, wept, and left.

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚怒，購求獲疇，謂曰：「汝不送章報我，何也？

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan was angry, offered reward and captured Chou, said: "You did not bring me the memorial report—why?
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan was furious. He put a price on Tian Chou's head, seized him, and demanded, "Why did you not bring me the court's reply?

sentences.zh: 」疇曰：「漢室衰頹，人懷異心，唯劉公不失忠節。

translations.literal: " Chou said: "The Han house declines, men harbor other hearts—only Lord Liu does not lose loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou answered, "The Han dynasty is failing. Men everywhere turn traitor. Only Lord Liu has kept faith.

sentences.zh: 章報所言，於將軍未美，恐非所樂聞，故不進也。

translations.literal: What the memorial report states would not flatter you, General—I feared it was not what you would wish to hear, so I did not present it.
translations.idiomatic: What the memorial says would not please you, General. I feared it was nothing you wished to hear, and so I did not bring it to you."

sentences.zh: 且將軍既滅無罪之君，又讎守義之臣，疇恐燕、趙之士皆將蹈東海而死，莫有從將軍者也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the general has already destroyed an innocent lord and made an enemy of a minister who kept faith; Chou fears that the gentlemen of Yan and Zhao will all throw themselves into the eastern sea to die, and none will follow the general.
translations.idiomatic: You have already killed an innocent lord and made an enemy of a faithful minister. I fear the men of Yan and Zhao will drown themselves in the eastern sea rather than follow you.

sentences.zh: 」瓚乃釋之。

translations.literal: " Zan thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan released him.

sentences.zh: 疇北歸無終，率宗族及他附從者數百人，掃地而盟曰：「君仇不報，吾不可立於世！

translations.literal: Chou returned north to Wuzhong, leading his clan and several hundred others who had attached themselves to him; they swept the ground and swore an oath: "If our lord's wrong is not avenged, I cannot stand in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou returned north to Wuzhong with his clan and several hundred followers. They swept the ground and swore: "Unless we avenge our lord, we have no place in this world!"

sentences.zh: 」遂入徐無山中，營深險平敞地而居，躬耕以養父母，百姓歸之，數年間至五千餘家。

translations.literal: " He then entered Mount Xuwu, chose a site deep, perilous, level, and open to dwell in, and personally plowed the fields to support his parents; the common people came to him, and within a few years they numbered more than five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew into Mount Xuwu, settled on a defensible plateau, and farmed to support his parents. Within a few years more than five thousand households had joined him.

sentences.zh: 疇謂其父老曰：「今眾成都邑，而莫相統一，又無法制以治之，恐非久安之道。

translations.literal: Chou said to the elders: "Now the multitude has formed a settlement, yet none unites the rest, and there are no laws and institutions to govern them—I fear this is not a path to lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou told the elders: "We have built a settlement but lack unity and law. That cannot last.

sentences.zh: 疇有愚計，願與諸君共施之，可乎？

translations.literal: Chou has a humble plan and wishes to carry it out together with you all—may I?
translations.idiomatic: I have a plan. Will you join me in putting it into practice?

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「可！

translations.literal: " All said: "We may!"
translations.idiomatic: They all agreed.

sentences.zh: 」疇乃為約束，相殺傷、犯盜、諍訟者，隨輕重抵罪，重者至死，凡一十餘條。

translations.literal: " Chou then drew up regulations: for mutual wounding, theft, and quarrelsome litigation, punishment was meted according to severity, the gravest reaching death—in all more than ten articles.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou drew up regulations: assault, theft, and litigation were punished by degree, up to death—more than ten articles in all.

sentences.zh: 又制為婚姻嫁娶之禮，與學校講授之業，班行於眾，眾皆便之，至道不拾遺。

translations.literal: He also instituted rites for marriage and betrothal, and the work of schools for lecturing and instruction, promulgating them among the multitude; all found them convenient, and on the roads nothing lost was picked up.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted marriage rites and schools for instruction. The people accepted them readily, and lost goods lay untouched on the roads.

sentences.zh: 北邊翕然服其威信，烏桓、鮮卑各遣使致饋，疇悉撫納，令不為寇。

translations.literal: The northern frontier submitted as one to his authority and prestige; the Wuhuan and Xianbei each sent envoys with gifts, and Chou received and comforted them all, ordering that they not raid.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes submitted to his authority. The Wuhuan and Xianbei sent envoys with gifts; Tian Chou received them and forbade raiding.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛丑，地震。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinchou, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinchou day, an earthquake struck.

sentences.zh: 司空趙溫免。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhao Wen was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhao Wen was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以衛尉張喜為司空。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the Commandant of Guards Zhang Xi was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day Zhang Xi, Commandant of Guards, was appointed Minister of Works.
